modules.title: Card
modules.description: The bordered surface each feature on a screen lives in, with an optional header and footer.
modules.importLine: import { Card, type CardProps } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
The bordered surface every feature on a screen lives in: an optional header
(title, subtitle, header actions), a padded body, and an optional footer. A
screen is a `<Page>` holding a vertical stack of Cards, one per feature. It can
also be a whole clickable list row (`size="small"` with `onClick`).

Use something else for: a "nothing here" block on the bare page (`EmptyState`),
a disclosure section with no card chrome (`CollapsibleSection`), a modal
(`Modal` / `ConfirmModal` in `@korzun/design/control`).

## Usage

The header renders only if one of `title`, `subTitle`, `headerAction`,
`onClickHeader`, or `isCollapsible` is set.

### Surprising behaviour

- **Keyboard on `onClick` is incomplete.** The root gets no `role` or
  `tabIndex`, so it is not focusable; its `onKeyDown` fires `onClick` on
  Enter/Space bubbling up from *any* focused child (an input inside a clickable
  card triggers it). Don't put form fields inside a clickable card.
- A header click on a collapsible card bubbles to the root, so `isCollapsible`
  together with `onClick` fires both.
- Collapsed content is unmounted, not hidden: child state resets on reopen.

### Corners

The corner follows depth: `radius.lg` on the page, `md` for a Card inside a
Card, `sm` deeper. A Card provides the next depth to its header, body and
footer, so nested Cards step down and Buttons inside take the matching radius
automatically (8px in a Card on a Page). See [corners](../corners.md).
`size="small"` insets its body by only 1px, so its corner is `calc(radius.md + 1px)`
(9px) on a page and `calc(radius.sm + 1px)` (5px) inside a Card: concentric with the `md`-cornered covers and rows flush inside it.

## Do / don't

- Do give each feature on a screen its own Card, stacked directly in `<Page>`.
- Do put row actions that must not fire by accident in `footer` of a
  collapsible card; they are unreachable while it is collapsed.
- Don't nest Cards just to group content; use `Divider`. When you do nest, corners step down automatically.
- Don't set `radius` on Buttons inside a Card: it follows depth, and an explicit `radius="card"` would stay 8px inside a nested Card, breaking the concentric corners.
- Don't expect `isCollapsible` cards to start open; pass `defaultCollapsed={false}`.
- Do use the exported `CardProps` type when wrapping Card.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description:
A feature on a screen: `title`, a `subTitle`, a `headerAction`, a form in the body and its
submit button in the `footer`. The footer button reaches the form by `form` id, so it submits it.

examples.title: Collapsible
examples.description:
`isCollapsible` turns the header into a toggle. A collapsible card starts collapsed, so the first
one is closed; pass `defaultCollapsed={false}` to start open, as the second one does. The
footer's destructive action is only reachable while the card is open.

examples.title: Clickable rows
examples.description:
`size="small"` with `onClick` makes a whole-card list row: a pointer cursor and only 1px of body
padding, so the child supplies its own padding and corner. A `CardRow` inside is flush with the
card and concentric with it. Clicking anywhere on a row fires `onClick`.

examples.title: Header click
examples.description: `onClickHeader` makes the header clickable. A click in `headerAction` does not reach it.

examples.title: Nested cards
examples.description:
A Card inside a Card steps its corner down one level: `lg` on the page, `md` inside a Card,
`sm` one level deeper. Each Card's Button follows the same depth, so pass no `radius`. Nest
for a group that is itself a feature; to split one body into sections use `Divider`.

changelog.text: `CardDivider` is now `Divider` and works anywhere: directly in a Card or Dialog body it reaches the edges as before (cancelling `space.xl` in a large Card, 1px in a small one, `space.xxl` in a Dialog, where it used to overhang everything but a large Card), and on the page, in a `CardRow`, `Alert`, `Surface` or nested Card it spans its container. The new `bleed` prop overrides that. **Breaking:** the old names `CardDivider`, `CardDividerProps` and `CardDividerAlign` are removed; import `Divider`, `DividerProps` and `DividerAlign`.

Surface depth: corners are concentric site-wide with no radius props. `Page` provides depth 0, `Dialog` 1, and `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` each provide one level deeper than where they sit; `Popover` (so `Menu` and the `Select` list) provides a fixed 2. Depth 0 is `radius.lg`, 1 is `md`, 2 and deeper is `sm`. `Button`, `Select`, `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` follow it; an explicit `Button radius` or `Select surface` still wins. With no `Page`, `Dialog`, `Card`, `CardRow`, `Alert` or `Surface` above it, a component keeps its 0.4.0 look; a bare `Card` (no `Page`) still counts as depth 0 and gives its contents depth 1, so its Buttons and nested Cards change as below.

**Visible changes:**
  - Buttons in a Card default to 8px (they were 16px unless `radius="card"` was set), and Buttons in a Dialog body are 8px.
  - Selects directly on a Page get the page look (16px and the card shadow); in a Card or Dialog they stay 8px. This includes Selects in your own boxes on a Page (a `useModalDialog` modal, a `recipe.card.shell` or `recipe.row` box), because depth cannot see hand-drawn boxes: wrap their contents in `Surface`, or pass `surface="card"`.
  - Without a Page, a bare `Card` counts as depth 0: its Buttons go from 16px to 8px, a Card nested in it steps down, and a `CardRow` in it is 8px.
  - A Card nested in a Card or Dialog steps down (8px, then 4px), and so do its Buttons and Selects; `size="small"` keeps its extra 1px.
  - `CardRow` is 16px on a Page and 8px inside a Card (it was always 16px).
  - Buttons and Selects inside a Popover or Menu are 4px.

`CardRow` drops its off-scale `12px` corner and takes `radius.lg` from the card shell, since a row sits on the page background. Its stories now render it on the page, not inside a `Card`. **Visible change:** the corners get rounder (12px to 16px).
`Card size="small"` writes its corner as `calc(radius.md + 1px)`: md plus its 1px inset, concentric with its flush `md` children. Same 9px as before, now derived from the token.

modules.title: CardRow
modules.description: A compact card-shell row for a stack of list items, optionally clickable.
modules.importLine: import { CardRow, type CardRowProps } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A compact card-shell row (card background, border, stacked shadow, 6px
padding) that sits on the page or in a Card, for a stack of list items. Optionally
clickable.

Use something else for: a shaded row inside a `Card` body (a row built on
`theme.recipe.row`), a section split (`Divider`), a key/value line
(`MetaLine` with labelled pairs). Bookplate itself lists items with `<Card size="small" onClick>`.

## Usage

### Styling

No `className`, no `ariaLabel`, no `role`.

### Surprising behaviour

- **Not keyboard-reachable.** With `onClick` it still gets no `role="button"`
  and no `tabIndex`, so it cannot be focused; the Enter/Space handler only
  fires for keys bubbling from a focused child, and Space is not
  `preventDefault`ed (the page scrolls). For a keyboard-accessible clickable
  row, put a real control (`Button type="link"`) inside it.
- Bookplate itself does not use `CardRow`; it is the least-exercised layout
  primitive here.

### Corners

Follows depth: 16px (`radius.lg`) on the page, 8px (`md`) in a Card, `sm`
deeper. Content inside it steps down one level. See [corners](../corners.md).

## Do / don't

- Place it on the page or inside a `Card`; its corners follow.
- Don't rely on `onClick` as the only way to reach an action from the keyboard.

modules.title: CollapsibleSection
modules.description: A disclosure section with no card chrome: a muted header with a chevron, optional count and actions, and children shown only while open.
modules.importLine: import { CollapsibleSection, type CollapsibleSectionProps } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A disclosure section with no card chrome: an uppercase, muted header row with a
text chevron (▶ / ▼), an optional count-style subtitle, optional trailing
actions, and children shown only while open. The header is a
`role="button"` (`tabIndex=0`, Enter/Space).

Use something else for: a collapsible feature on a screen (`Card` with
`isCollapsible`, which also hides its footer while collapsed).

## Usage

### Controlled and uncontrolled

Omit `open` and the section keeps its own state, always starting closed; there
is no `defaultOpen`. Pass `open` and flip your own state in `onOpenToggle`,
which receives no value.

When controlled, `open` wins but the internal state still flips on every
click; if you later stop passing `open`, the section shows that stale internal
state.

### Actions

- Actions are rendered inside the header button, but clicks and key presses
  inside an action stay with it: any action (a `Button`, a native `<button>`, a
  link, a `Chip` with `onClick`) works without toggling the section, and Enter or
  Space on it activates the action, not the header.
- Actions in the array need their own `key`s (they are rendered as a bare
  array).

### Accessibility

The header has no `aria-expanded`.

### Styling

No `className`.

## Do / don't

- Do pass `actions` as an array of keyed elements.
- Don't use it as a screen's top-level feature container; that is `Card`.

modules.title: Divider
modules.description: A horizontal rule that splits content into sections, optionally labelled and with actions; in a Card or Modal body it reaches the edges.
modules.importLine: import { Divider, type DividerAlign, type DividerProps } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A horizontal rule that splits content into sections, optionally with a label
("Devices", "Validation") and/or actions sitting on the line. Directly inside a
`Card` or `Modal` body it cancels the body's padding, so the line meets the
box's edges; anywhere else it spans its container. Renders `role="separator"`.

Use something else for: separating whole features (use separate `Card`s),
separating menu items (`PageActionItem.separatorBefore`).

## Usage

### Styling

No `className`.

### Surprising behaviour

- **The bleed only reaches the nearest body.** A divider bleeds when the Card
  or Modal body is the nearest box around it. Inside a `CardRow`, `Alert`,
  `Surface` or nested `Card` it spans that box instead. `bleed={false}` opts
  out in a body; `bleed` does nothing outside one.
- **A padded wrapper defeats it.** In a Card body but inside your own padded
  `div`, the divider still cancels the Card's padding, not yours. Wrap the
  box's contents in `Surface`, or pass `bleed={false}`.
- It always reserves one label line of height, labelled or not, so swapping a
  plain divider for a labelled one does not shift the layout.
- The label does not wrap (`white-space: nowrap`); keep it to a word or two.

## Do / don't

- Do put it straight in a Card body, or in a `Space` there, not in a padded
  `div`.
- Do use `type="link"` Buttons or small `Chip`s as `actions`; the line is one
  text line tall.
- Don't use it for the gap between Cards on a page; `Page` already spaces them.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description:
A plain rule between a form's fields and its submit button. Directly in a Card body it cancels
the body's padding, so the line meets the Card's borders.

examples.title: Labelled
examples.description:
A label names the section below the line. `align` places it: `left` and `right` hug that edge
with a short stub of line past it, `center` leaves equal line on both sides.

examples.title: Actions
examples.description:
`actions` puts controls on the line: use link Buttons, the line is one text line tall.
`actionsAlign` places them on the `left`, `center` or `right`. When it equals `align` the label
and the actions share one group, label first. Each divider is captioned with its props.
examples.code:
import { Card, Divider, Space, Text } from '@korzun/design/component';
import { Button } from '@korzun/design/control';
import { useState } from 'react';

export default function Actions() {
  const [pending, setPending] = useState(['Middlemarch', 'Persuasion']);
  const [last, setLast] = useState('nothing yet');
  return (
    <Card title="Requests">
      <Space direction="vertical" gap="xl">
        <Space direction="vertical" gap="xs">
          <Text size="sm" tone="muted">
            Unset: label left, actions right
          </Text>
          <Divider
            actions={
              <Button type="link" onClick={() => setPending([])}>
                Clear all
              </Button>
            }
          >
            Pending
          </Divider>
          <Text>{pending.length > 0 ? pending.join(', ') : 'Nothing pending'}</Text>
        </Space>
        <Space direction="vertical" gap="xs">
          <Text size="sm" tone="muted">
            {'align="center" actionsAlign="left"'}
          </Text>
          <Divider
            align="center"
            actionsAlign="left"
            actions={
              <Button type="link" onClick={() => setLast('Archive')}>
                Archive
              </Button>
            }
          >
            Finished
          </Divider>
        </Space>
        <Space direction="vertical" gap="xs">
          <Text size="sm" tone="muted">
            {'align="right" actionsAlign="right": one group, label first'}
          </Text>
          <Divider
            align="right"
            actionsAlign="right"
            actions={
              <Button type="link" onClick={() => setLast('Share')}>
                Share
              </Button>
            }
          >
            Shared
          </Divider>
        </Space>
        <Text tone="muted">Last action: {last}</Text>
      </Space>
    </Card>
  );
}

examples.title: Outside a Card
examples.description:
Anywhere but directly in a Card or Modal body (on the page, in a CardRow, a hand-made
`Surface` box or a Popover) the line spans its container. In a Card body it reaches the
borders; `bleed={false}` keeps it inside the padding there.
examples.code:
import { Card, CardRow, Divider, Space, Text } from '@korzun/design/component';

export default function Anywhere() {
  return (
    <Space direction="vertical" gap="xl">
      <Space direction="vertical" gap="xs">
        <Text size="sm" tone="muted">
          On the page: spans the column
        </Text>
        <Divider>Devices</Divider>
        <Text>Kitchen frame, Hallway frame</Text>
      </Space>
      <Card title="Notifications">
        <Space direction="vertical">
          <Text size="sm" tone="muted">
            In the Card body: meets the borders
          </Text>
          <Divider />
          <Text size="sm" tone="muted">
            {'bleed={false}: inside the padding'}
          </Text>
          <Divider bleed={false} />
          <CardRow>
            <Space direction="vertical" gap="xs">
              <Text size="sm" tone="muted">
                In a CardRow: spans the row
              </Text>
              <Divider />
              <Text>Keep notifications for 30 days.</Text>
            </Space>
          </CardRow>
        </Space>
      </Card>
    </Space>
  );
}

modules.title: Page
modules.description: The `<main>` of every screen: a centred column of Cards, plus back button, header and footer actions.
modules.importLine: import { Page, type PageProps, type PageTypeValue } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
The `<main>` of every screen: a centred 800px column (gutter `space.xxl`) that
stacks its children vertically with a fixed gap. A screen is a `Page` holding a
vertical stack of `Card`s, one per feature. Page also owns the screen's chrome:
the mobile back button, the header actions (a bar on desktop, a floating `⋯`
menu on mobile), and the footer actions row.

Use something else for: a sign-in or splash screen with no chrome
(`type="minimal"` here, then lay it out yourself), a section inside a screen
(`Card`).

## Usage

### Header slot

`header` is the page's own content for the header row, the row the desktop
actions bar occupies. Pass a search bar there rather than rendering it as the
first child: as a child it would sit below the reserved row and start this page
lower than every other page.

### Behaviour

- Page marks everything inside it (header, content, footer actions, every `type`) as surface depth 0, so controls and cards inside pick their corner radius from where they sit; see `Surface`.
- **The header row is always reserved on default pages**, even with no actions
  and no `header` (min-height `2.25rem` on desktop), so content starts at the
  same height on every page. On mobile the row collapses (`display: contents`).
- On mobile the back button and the actions menu sit in a **sticky** row at the
  top that rides up with the page and then pins (at
  `theme.layout.floatingControlTopBase`); it also renders on `minimal` pages
  if you pass `back` or `headerActions`.
- `footerActions` is a plain `PageFooterActions` row after the children. It is
  not sticky.
- The column gap is `theme.fontSize.md` (0.875rem), a historical value, not a
  `space` token.
- `PageActionItem` and `FooterAction` are exported from
  `@korzun/design/control`, not from `component`.
- No `className`.

## Do / don't

- Do make each feature its own `Card`, as direct children of `Page`.
- Do pass `bottomNav` on every page shown under `NavMobile`.
- Do mark the one or two main actions `primary: true` so desktop shows them as
  buttons rather than burying them in "More…".
- Don't render your own search bar as the first child; use `header`.
- Don't wrap Page in another `<main>`; it is the `<main>`.
- Don't rely on `back` for desktop navigation.

header row stays reserved above the first card even with no actions, so every

`bottomNav` reserves space under the content so the last card clears the

`type="minimal"` drops the page's width, margin, padding, gap and header row,

changelog.text: Surface depth: corners are concentric site-wide with no radius props. `Page` provides depth 0, `Dialog` 1, and `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` each provide one level deeper than where they sit; `Popover` (so `Menu` and the `Select` list) provides a fixed 2. Depth 0 is `radius.lg`, 1 is `md`, 2 and deeper is `sm`. `Button`, `Select`, `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` follow it; an explicit `Button radius` or `Select surface` still wins. With no `Page`, `Dialog`, `Card`, `CardRow`, `Alert` or `Surface` above it, a component keeps its 0.4.0 look; a bare `Card` (no `Page`) still counts as depth 0 and gives its contents depth 1, so its Buttons and nested Cards change as below.

**Visible changes:**
  - Buttons in a Card default to 8px (they were 16px unless `radius="card"` was set), and Buttons in a Dialog body are 8px.
  - Selects directly on a Page get the page look (16px and the card shadow); in a Card or Dialog they stay 8px. This includes Selects in your own boxes on a Page (a `useModalDialog` modal, a `recipe.card.shell` or `recipe.row` box), because depth cannot see hand-drawn boxes: wrap their contents in `Surface`, or pass `surface="card"`.
  - Without a Page, a bare `Card` counts as depth 0: its Buttons go from 16px to 8px, a Card nested in it steps down, and a `CardRow` in it is 8px.
  - A Card nested in a Card or Dialog steps down (8px, then 4px), and so do its Buttons and Selects; `size="small"` keeps its extra 1px.
  - `CardRow` is 16px on a Page and 8px inside a Card (it was always 16px).
  - Buttons and Selects inside a Popover or Menu are 4px.

modules.title: PageActionsBar
modules.description: The desktop page-actions row: primary actions as inline buttons and the rest in an overflow menu.
modules.importLine: import { PageActionsBar, type PageActionsBarProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
The desktop page-actions row: `primary` items render as inline Buttons and
the rest collapse into a "More…" overflow menu. It is hidden at 640px and
below, where [`PageActionsMenu`](page-actions-menu.md) shows the same items.
Usually you don't render it yourself: pass `headerActions` (and `actionsLabel`)
to `Page`, which puts it in the header row.

Use something else for: mobile ([`PageActionsMenu`](page-actions-menu.md)),
bottom-of-page form actions (`PageFooterActions`), a one-off button inside a
card ([`Button`](button.md)). For any other actions-behind-a-button, use
[`Menu`](menu.md).

## Usage

### How items are placed

`PageActionItem` is the shape [`PageActionsMenu`](page-actions-menu.md) shares:
see its [item table](page-actions-menu.md#pageactionitem).

- `primary: true` → an inline [`Button`](button.md) (`type="default"`, its
  radius following the surface depth, so `radius.lg` on the page background).
  `align: 'leading'` puts it at the left; anything else is trailing, at the
  right. `danger` and `disabled` apply.
- Not primary → the overflow menu (solid card surface, `radius.md`, items
  `radius.sm`), opened by the trigger at the far right. `separatorBefore`
  draws a divider there.
- No overflow items → no trigger.
- **`Icon` and `intentProps` only work on overflow items**; primary Buttons drop
  them.
- Items are keyed by `label`, so labels must be unique.

### Behaviour to know

- The overflow is a `Menu` (`surface="solid" align="end"`), so it has Menu's
  keyboard behaviour. Opening focuses the first enabled item. Up and Down move
  through enabled items and wrap; Home and End jump to the ends; Enter and
  Space activate.
- Selecting an item closes the menu, returns focus to the trigger, then calls
  `onClick`. Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger. Tab closes and
  moves on from the trigger. A mousedown outside closes without moving focus.
- Escape and outside presses go to the innermost open layer first: a Select
  opened over the menu closes before the menu does.
- The trigger is a native `<button>` with `aria-haspopup="menu"`,
  `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. The menu renders in a
  [`Popover`](popover.md), `space.sm` under the trigger, right-aligned to it.
- The bar has no `className`.

## Do / don't

- Do mark at most two or three items `primary`; the rest belong in the menu.
- Do use `Page headerActions` so the mobile menu gets the same items.
- Don't rely on `intentProps` for a primary item.

modules.title: PageActionsMenu
modules.description: The mobile page-actions control: a round glass button that opens a menu of every page action.
modules.importLine: import { PageActionsMenu, type PageActionIntentProps, type PageActionItem, type PageActionsMenuProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
The mobile page-actions control: a round glass "More actions" button (⋯)
that opens a glass menu listing every action. It is hidden at 641px and up,
where [`PageActionsBar`](page-actions-bar.md) takes over with the same items.
Usually you don't render it yourself: pass `headerActions` to `Page`, which
renders both.

Use something else for: desktop header actions
([`PageActionsBar`](page-actions-bar.md)), bottom-of-page form actions
(`PageFooterActions`), a single inline action ([`Button`](button.md)). For any
other actions-behind-a-button, use [`Menu`](menu.md).

## Usage

### The trigger

The trigger is always the round "More actions" button: there is no label prop
and no `className`.

### Items

`PageActionItem` is shared with `PageActionsBar`, so one array drives both. It is
[`Menu`](menu.md)'s action item (`MenuActionItem`) plus `primary` and `align`,
which only `PageActionsBar` uses; this menu ignores them. `to` is not allowed:
page actions are actions, not links. The tables under Props list each field.

### Behaviour to know

- It is a `Menu` (`surface="glass" align="end"`), so it has Menu's keyboard
  behaviour. Opening focuses the first enabled item. Up and Down move through
  enabled items and wrap; Home and End jump to the ends; Enter and Space
  activate.
- Selecting an item closes the menu, returns focus to the trigger, then calls
  `onClick`. Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger. Tab closes and
  moves on from the trigger. A mousedown outside closes without moving focus.
- Escape and outside presses go to the innermost open layer first: a Select
  opened over the menu closes before the menu does.
- The menu is a floating layer (`radius.md`, glass, items `radius.sm`) in a
  [`Popover`](popover.md) portalled to the body, `space.sm` under the trigger,
  right-aligned to it; it flips above when there is no room below.
- It doesn't place itself: `Page` puts it in the sticky controls row
  (`margin-left: auto` keeps it at the trailing end, with or without a
  `BackButton`).

## Do / don't

- Do pass the same `items` you give `PageActionsBar` (or just use `Page`).
- Do put destructive items last with `separatorBefore`.
- Don't render it on its own and expect it on desktop; it is hidden there.
- Don't give two items the same `label`; they collide as React keys.

modules.title: PageFooterActions
modules.description: A row of Buttons for the bottom of a page, split into leading and trailing sides.
modules.importLine: import { PageFooterActions, type FooterAction, type PageFooterActionsProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A row of Buttons for the bottom of a page, split into leading and trailing
sides: typically Cancel / Save for a form that spans several cards. Leading
items sit left, trailing items right. It is a plain flex row (not sticky, shown
at every width). `Page` renders it after its children when you pass
`footerActions`; you can also render it directly after your form.

Use something else for: header actions (`PageActionsBar` / `PageActionsMenu`
via `Page headerActions`), a Card's own submit (`Button` in the Card `footer`),
modal buttons (`Modal` footer).

## Usage

### Submitting a form

The row sits outside the form, below the cards, so a submit item needs `form`
(the id of the `<form>`) as well as `submit`. `onClick` is required on every
item but is never called for a submit one; the form's `action` or `onSubmit`
runs instead. Drive `loading` and `disabled` from your own pending and
validation state.

### Corners

The Buttons follow surface depth: the row sits on the page background below the
cards, so on a `Page` they get the page's 16px corners; see
[corners](../corners.md). No `className`.

## Do / don't

- Do give exactly one item `emphasis`.
- Do pair `submit` with `form` when the row is outside the `<form>`.
- Don't put a destructive action beside Save without `danger` and
  `align: 'leading'`.
- Don't put PageFooterActions inside a `Card`; a Card's own submit goes in its
  `footer`.

modules.title: Space
modules.description: One layout primitive: a row or a column with a themed gap between children and an optional separator.
modules.importLine: import { Space, type Gap, type SpaceProps } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A flex row or column with a themed gap between children. Use it to space
things on a screen instead of writing a style file: a button group, a form's
fields, a header with an action on the right, a line of items split by dots.

Use something else for: a bordered surface (`Card`), a divider line between
items (`Divider`), text styling (`Text`, `Heading`).

## Usage

### Direction and defaults

`direction` is `'horizontal'` (a row, the default) or `'vertical'` (a column).
Each direction has its own defaults:

| | `gap` | `align` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `horizontal` | `sm` | `center` |
| `vertical` | `md` | `stretch` |

### Choosing a gap

Pick `gap` from the theme's `space` scale so spacing is the same everywhere:
`xs` for tight groups such as chips, `sm` for most rows, `md` for most
columns, `xxl` between sections. `gap="none"` emits `gap: 0`, for children
that supply their own spacing.

### Split

`split` draws a separator between each pair of children, never before the
first or after the last. Children that render nothing (`null`, `false`, `''`, an
empty fragment) get no separator, and a fragment's children count as separate
items. The separator is hidden from screen readers. Inside `as="ul"` or
`as="ol"` it is an `li` with `role="presentation"`, so the list stays valid.

### Wrap and justify

- `wrap` lets children flow onto further lines. Without it they stay on one
  line and may overflow or shrink.
- `justify="between"` pushes the first and last child to opposite edges: a
  title with an action on the right.

### Behaviour

- `as="ul"` and `as="ol"` also reset the list's margin, padding and bullets.
  Children should be `li`.
- `align` is the cross axis: vertical placement in a row, horizontal in a
  column. `start` keeps buttons and tags at their own width in a column.
- Every other HTML attribute (`id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event handlers) passes
  through. There is no `style` prop: spacing comes from tokens only.
- Override with `className` at `'&&'` specificity, never `!important`.
- `as="form"` is not offered. Put a `<form>` around the Space instead.

### Coming from Stack or Inline

`<Stack …>` is `<Space direction="vertical" …>`, and `<Inline …>` is
`<Space …>`. Every other prop and default is the same.

## Do / don't

- Do use `direction="vertical"` for a form's fields or a page's sections.
- Do use `justify="between"` for a title-and-action row.
- Do add `wrap` for rows of chips or buttons that may not fit on a phone.
- Do use `split` for separators instead of inserting your own between items.
- Don't add margins to children to space them; use `gap`.
- Don't nest a row just to push one child right; use `justify="between"`.

changelog.text: New `Space`: one layout primitive with a `direction` (default `'horizontal'`), `gap`, `align`, `justify`, `wrap`, `as` and a `split` separator drawn between items (hidden from screen readers, an `li` inside a list). Each direction keeps Stack's or Inline's defaults.

**Breaking:** `Stack` and `Inline` (and `StackProps`, `InlineProps`) are removed; use `Space`. `<Stack …>` is `<Space direction="vertical" …>` and `<Inline …>` is `<Space …>`, with every prop and default unchanged.

New `Stack` (vertical flex column; `gap`, default `md`), `Inline` (horizontal row; `gap` default `sm`, `justify` including `between`), `Text` (`size`, `tone`, `weight`; unset props inherit), and `Heading` (`level` 1–4), so layout and text are set with props instead of style files.
`truncate` on `Text` and `Heading` clips inside `Stack` (any `align`), `Inline`, and a `Stack` nested in an `Inline`; `Stack` and `Inline` roots have `min-width: 0`.

modules.title: Surface
modules.description: Marks a hand-made box as one more level of nesting, so the library controls inside it take the next corner radius down.
modules.importLine: import { Surface, useSurfaceRadius, type SurfaceProps } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
Marks a hand-made box as one more level of nesting. Every library control
inside it (`Button`, `Select`, `Card`, `CardRow`, ...) takes its corner radius
from how deep it sits, following the one-radius-step-per-level rule in
[corners](../corners.md). `Page` marks its whole area as depth 0, `Modal` as
depth 1, and `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` each one level deeper than where
they sit. `Surface` adds one more level for a box you draw yourself.

Wrap the box's contents, not the box: the box itself takes the surrounding depth.

Use `Surface` when you build your own bordered or filled box that contains
library controls. Do not use it around a library `Card`, `CardRow` or `Modal`;
they already count themselves.

## Usage

### `useSurfaceRadius()`

```ts
useSurfaceRadius(): string
```

Returns the radius string (a theme `radius` token) for the current depth. Call
it in the component that draws the box, outside its own `Surface`: the box
then gets the radius for where it sits, and `Surface` steps the controls inside
it one level deeper. With no `Page`, `Modal`, `Card`, `CardRow`, `Alert` or
`Surface` above it, it returns the depth 0 radius.

### Depth table

| Depth | Radius                       | Where                                    |
| ----- | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| 0     | `radius.lg`                  | on the page background                   |
| 1     | `radius.md`                  | inside a Card or Modal                  |
| 2+    | `radius.sm`                  | inside a surface inside a Card or Modal |
| none  | each component's own default | no Page, Modal, Card, CardRow, Alert or Surface above it |

Depth never goes below `sm`; deeper nesting stays at `sm`. Hand-drawn boxes are invisible to depth, so wrap their contents in `Surface`.

### Styling

`Surface` renders no element of its own, so it has no `className`.

## Do / don't

- Do wrap the contents of a hand-made box that holds library controls in `Surface`.
- Do take the box's own radius from `useSurfaceRadius()`, never a literal.
- Don't wrap library `Card`, `CardRow` or `Modal` in `Surface`.

Depth 0 is `radius.lg`, 1 is `md`, 2 and deeper is `sm`. `Button`, `Select`, `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` follow it; an explicit `Button radius` or `Select surface` still wins. With no `Page`, `Dialog`, `Card`, `CardRow`, `Alert` or `Surface` above it, a component keeps its 0.4.0 look; a bare `Card` (no `Page`) still counts as depth 0 and gives its contents depth 1, so its Buttons and nested Cards change as below.

modules.title: TopFade
modules.description: A decorative, mobile-only frosted scrim at the top of the viewport that blurs content scrolling under the status bar.
modules.importLine: import { TopFade, type TopFadeProps } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A decorative, mobile-only scrim: a `position: fixed` frosted-glass band at the
top of the viewport, as tall as the status-bar safe-area inset plus
`space.md`, that blurs content scrolling under the device status bar and fades
to nothing below it (Safari style). It is `aria-hidden`,
`pointer-events: none`, and hidden at `min-width: 641px`.

Use something else for: a header or toolbar (`Page` header row / actions),
dimming behind a modal (the modal's own backdrop).

## Usage

### When to render it

- **Only in the installed (standalone) app**, gated with `useIsStandalone()` from
  `@korzun/design/hooks`. In a browser tab the OS status bar is not drawn over
  the page, `env(safe-area-inset-top)` is 0, and the band would be a thin
  blurred strip with no purpose.
- Once, in the layout route, not per page.
- It sits at `theme.zIndex.header`: above page content, below the floating
  controls and nav (`zIndex.sticky`).

```tsx
// Layout route for nav-bearing pages.
export const NavLayout = () => {
  const standalone = useIsStandalone();
  return (
    <>
      <NavDesktop items={items} />
      <NavMobile main={…} settings={…} expanded={…} />
      {standalone && (
        <>
          <TopFade />
          <PullToRefreshIndicator /> {/* your own, built on usePullToRefresh */}
        </>
      )}
      <Outlet />
    </>
  );
};
```

### Behaviour

- It takes no props and no `className`.
- Its height comes from `env(safe-area-inset-top)`, which is non-zero only when
  the page opts into the safe area (`<meta name="viewport"
  content="…, viewport-fit=cover">`). Without that it is `space.md` tall.
- The tail is deliberately short so chrome resting near the top edge
  (`theme.layout.floatingControlTopBase`) is never drawn through the blur.
  Don't place your own content in the first `space.md` below the inset.

## Do / don't

- Do gate it on `useIsStandalone()`.
- Do render it once per app layout.
- Don't use it as a visual header; it carries no content and ignores clicks.

modules.title: Anchor
modules.description: A page outline that marks the section in view and scrolls to a section on click, as a list of titles or a minimap of dashes.
modules.importLine: import { Anchor, type AnchorItem, type AnchorProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A page outline that marks the section in view and scrolls to a section on
click, as a list of titles or a minimap of dashes. You pass the sections as
`items` (`{ id, title, level }`); it does not read headings from the page. It
renders a `nav` with a list of `<a href="#id">` links, so a link can still be
copied or opened in a new tab.

Use something else for: moving between screens (`NavDesktop`, `NavMobile`),
going up a level (`BackButton`), actions (`Menu`).

## Usage

### Choosing a look

- `variant="list"`: an indented list of titles, each level past 1 indented a
  step. The current one is blue with a bar on its left edge. Use it where a
  side column has room for the titles, as in a docs page.
- `variant="minimap"`: a slim column of dashes, one per item, 16px, 12px or
  8px wide by level. The current dash is blue. Hovering the dashes, or moving
  focus into them, opens the list in a card beside them, on their left, so
  keyboard users see the titles as they tab. It closes when the pointer and
  focus have both left; Escape closes one the pointer opened. Use it at the edge of a reading page, where a
  list would crowd the text, as Notion does. Clicking a dash scrolls to its
  section too.

Both looks are the same `nav` and the same links: the minimap only hides the
titles until it opens.

### The current section

The current section is the last item whose element's top is at or above
`offset + 1` px from the top of the window. Above the first item it is the
first; scrolled to the bottom of the page it is the last, so a short last
section can still be current. The link gets `aria-current="location"`. It is
recomputed on scroll and resize, at most once a frame.

An item whose `id` is not on the page is still listed, and clicking it does
nothing, but it is never current.

### Scrolling and focus

A click scrolls the window so the section's top sits `offset` px below the top
of the window: smoothly, or at once under `prefers-reduced-motion`. It then
moves focus to the section's element, adding `tabindex="-1"` if the element
has no `tabindex`, so the next Tab continues from there.

It never changes the URL: the click is handled in place of the browser's jump
to `#id`, because an app with hash routing (this docs site) would read the hash
as a route. A click with Ctrl, Cmd, Shift or Alt is left to the browser.

It scrolls the window only, not a scrolling element inside the page.

### Offset

`offset` is the height in px of sticky chrome above the content, such as a
sticky header. It is used both for where a click lands and for when a section
counts as current, so a section turns current as it passes under the header.
Measure the header rather than guess (the Placement example does).

### Placement and phones

Anchor never positions itself. Place it yourself:

- **Sticky in a side column**, beside the article: wrap it in an element with
  `position: sticky` and a `top`. This suits the list.
- **Fixed at the right edge**, vertically centred: wrap it in an element with
  `position: fixed`. This suits the minimap; its panel opens to the left,
  toward the page.

On phones there is usually no room beside the text: hide it with
`theme.breakpoint.mobile` (`display: 'none'`), as the Placement example does.

### Keyboard

Tab moves through the links, in both looks. Enter scrolls to the section and
moves focus to it. In the minimap, focus on a link opens the panel, and it
stays open while focus is inside, so the focused link stays visible: Tab past
the last link or Shift+Tab before the first to close it. Escape closes a panel
the pointer opened.

### Corners

The links' focus ring has a fixed `sm` radius, as Menu items do; the
minimap's panel is a `md` card, as a Popover is (see
[corners](../corners.md)).

### Styling

Takes `className` on the `nav`.

## Do / don't

- Do give every target element a unique `id` and pass items in page order.
- Do pass `offset` when a sticky header covers the top of the page, or clicks
  land under it.
- Don't put it in an element that scrolls on its own: it tracks and scrolls the
  window.

header, and a section turns current as it passes under it.

modules.title: BackButton
modules.description: A round glass "Back" button for mobile that navigates to a fixed path.
modules.importLine: import { BackButton, type BackButtonProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A round glass "Back" button that navigates to a fixed path. It is mobile-only:
at widths of 641px and up it renders `display: none`, because desktop has its
own navigation. Usually you don't render it yourself: pass `back` to `Page`.

Use something else for: any other action (`Button`), header actions
(`PageActionsMenu` / `PageActionsBar`, also via `Page`).

## Usage

### Navigation

- **It pushes `to`, it does not go back in history.** Click (or Enter / Space)
  calls `navigate(to, { state: { restoreScroll: true } })`: a new history entry,
  with a state flag asking the destination's scroll manager to restore its
  remembered position instead of jumping to the top.
- Requires a `react-router` (v8, a peer dependency) router above it; it calls
  `useNavigate()` and throws without one.

### Appearance

- Renders a `<div role="button" tabIndex={0} aria-label="Back">` with a
  left-pointing chevron, 46×46px, `radius.circle`, `recipe.glass`.
- It does not position itself. `Page` puts it in its sticky controls row; if
  you render it elsewhere, you place it.
- That is the whole API. No `className`, no label, no `onClick`.

## Do / don't

- Do use `Page back="…"` instead of rendering `BackButton` directly, so it lines
  up with the mobile actions menu.
- Do pass the logical parent route (`/library`, the book page), not a guess at
  the previous URL: it always goes to `to`.
- Don't expect it on desktop; it is hidden at 641px and up.
- Don't wrap it in a `<button>` or `<a>`, or try to restyle it: there is no
  `className`.

modules.title: NavDesktop
modules.description: The app's top navigation on wide screens: a centred row of icon and label links with the active one underlined.
modules.importLine: import { NavDesktop, type NavDesktopProps, type NavItem } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
The app's top navigation on wide screens: a centred row of icon + label links
on the page background, the active one underlined. Hidden below the mobile
breakpoint (`max-width: 640px`), so render it alongside `NavMobile` and let CSS
pick. Each item is a react-router `<Link>`, so it **must render inside a
router**.

Use something else for: mobile navigation (`NavMobile`), in-page tabs or a
mode switch (`SegmentedControl`), page-level actions (`Page` `headerActions`).

## Usage

### Items

Each item is a `NavItem`, shared with `NavMobile`; its fields are in the
generated tables below. `active` is yours to compute from the route, in one
place, and both navs take the same items:

```tsx
const { pathname } = useLocation();
const items: NavItem[] = [
  { to: '/library', label: 'Library', Icon: BookIcon, active: pathname.startsWith('/library') },
  { to: '/upload', label: 'Upload', Icon: UploadIcon, active: pathname === '/upload', badge: pendingFixes },
];

// In the layout route, above <Outlet />.
<NavDesktop items={items} />
<NavMobile main={{ items, collapsed: items[0] }} settings={…} expanded="main" />
<Outlet />
```

### Styling

No `className`.

### Behaviour to know

- It is **not** fixed or sticky; it is a normal `<header>` in flow at the top
  of the document, so render it before your routes' content.
- Badges are visual only: the count has no accessible label, and a dot has no
  text at all. Put the meaning in `label` if it matters to screen readers.

## Do / don't

- Do render both `NavDesktop` and `NavMobile`; each hides itself at the other's
  breakpoint.
- Do derive `active` from the current route in one place and share the items.
- Don't pass an element as `Icon` (`Icon: <HomeIcon />`); pass the component.
- Don't render it outside a react-router `Router`.

modules.title: NavMobile
modules.description: The app's bottom navigation on phones: two frosted pills, one expanded into tabs and one a circle.
modules.importLine: import { NavMobile, type NavMobileProps, type NavPill } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
The app's bottom navigation on phones: a `position: fixed` bar floating above
the bottom edge, holding two frosted-glass pills. The **expanded** side is a
capsule of tabs with a glass lens sliding to the active one; the other side is
a circle that links to a single destination. Scrolling down fast minimizes the
expanded side to a circle too (iOS-tab-bar style); scrolling up, reaching the
top, tapping the circle, or a route change brings it back. Hidden at
`min-width: 641px`, so render it alongside `NavDesktop`. Uses react-router
`Link` and `useLocation`, so it **must render inside a router**.

Use something else for: desktop navigation (`NavDesktop`), page actions
(`Page` `headerActions` / `footerActions`).

## Usage

### Sides and items

Each side is a `NavPill`: `items` are its tabs while it is the `expanded` side,
and `collapsed` is the one destination its circle links to. A tab is a
`NavItem`, documented with [NavDesktop](nav-desktop.md#navitem); tab icons are
drawn at 14px. Derive `expanded` and every `active` from the route in one place (`main` and `settingsItems` are `NavItem[]` lists as in [Expanded side](#expanded-side)):

```tsx
const { pathname } = useLocation();
const inSettings = pathname === '/settings' || pathname === '/users';

<NavMobile
  main={{ items: main, collapsed: { to: '/library', label: 'Back to library', Icon: HomeIcon, active: false } }}
  settings={{ items: settingsItems, collapsed: { to: '/settings', label: 'Settings', Icon: SettingsIcon, active: pathname === '/settings' } }}
  expanded={inSettings ? 'settings' : 'main'}
/>
```

### Styling

No `className`.

### Behaviour to know

- **The page must make room for it:** pass `bottomNav` to every `<Page>` that
  shows this bar, or the last rows sit under it. Toasts already clear it on
  mobile.
- Tabs are equal-width columns sized to the widest label. Five short labels fit
  at 320px; six do not (Bookplate measured "Library"/"Settings" clipping), so
  move extra destinations into the other side.
- The minimized circle is a `<button aria-label="Show navigation">`, not a
  link: tapping it only re-expands the bar. It shows the active tab's icon (or
  `collapsed.Icon` when no tab is active) and the active tab's badge, else a
  dot if any hidden sibling has a badge.
- Minimizing only reacts to user-driven scroll (after a touch or wheel on this
  route), so scroll restoration on navigation never minimizes it. Tuning
  constants live in [`useMinimizeOnScroll`](../hooks/use-minimize-on-scroll.md) (`MINIMIZE_SPEED`, `EXPAND_AFTER`).
- Hidden shapes are `inert` and `aria-hidden`; only what is on screen is in
  the tab order.
- A side with `items: []` is a circle for good (Bookplate does this for a
  non-admin's settings side).

## Do / don't

- Do render it once, in the layout route, next to `NavDesktop`.
- Do set `bottomNav` on each `Page` under that layout.
- Do drive `expanded` from the URL so Back behaves.
- Don't keep more than about five tabs on one side.
- Don't also call `useMinimizeOnScroll` for the same bar; NavMobile owns it.

modules.title: Code
modules.description: Inline code in the mono font, sized to the surrounding text, for a prop name or a short expression in a line of prose.
modules.importLine: import { Code, type CodeProps } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
Inline code in the mono font, sized to the surrounding text, for a prop name or
a short expression in a line of prose. It renders a `<code>` element at 0.875em
of the text around it, so it scales in a heading, on a tinted chip with
`space.xxs` side padding.

Use something else for: a block of several lines or a snippet to copy
(`CodeBlock`), a keyboard key or a status chip (`Chip`).

## Usage

### Styling

Takes `className`, merged last. The look is fixed: it is the same
`theme.recipe.inlineCode` that styles code in the docs' markdown.

### Surprising behaviour

- **Breaks only when it must.** A long name stays on its line and wraps
  (`overflow-wrap: break-word`) only when it cannot fit the line.
- **Dark mode adds an edge on the page only.** Directly on a `Page` in dark
  mode, a 1px `border.default` hairline separates the chip from the page. Inside
  a `Card`, `Modal` or other surface the tint reads on its own, so there is none.

### Corners

The chip's corners are fixed at `radius.sm` at every depth: it is a glyph
smaller than a line of text. See [corners](../corners.md).

## Do / don't

- Do use it for names and short expressions inside a sentence or a heading.
- Don't put a multi-line snippet in it; use `CodeBlock`.

modules.title: Heading
modules.description: A heading whose level sets the element and a default look, with size, tone and weight to override it.
modules.importLine: import { Heading, type HeadingProps } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A heading. `level` is the semantics (which `h1` to `h4` element renders) and
also picks a default look; `size`, `tone` and `weight` are the look and
override those defaults. Use it for a page title, a section title, a card
title.

Use something else for: body or meta text (`Text`), a collapsible section
header (`CollapsibleSection`), an empty-state title (`EmptyState`).

## Usage

### Level defaults

| `level` | Element | `size` | `weight`   |
| ------- | ------- | ------ | ---------- |
| 1       | `h1`    | `xxl`  | `bold`     |
| 2       | `h2`    | `xl`   | `bold`     |
| 3       | `h3`    | `lg`   | `semibold` |
| 4       | `h4`    | `md`   | `semibold` |

Tone is `primary` at every level. A `size` or `weight` you set wins over the
level default.

### Behaviour

- **Level is the semantics, props are the look.** Pick `level` for the document
  outline (one `h1` per page, no skipped levels), then use `size`, `weight` and
  `tone` to change how it looks. Never pick a level for its size.
- The margin is reset to 0 and the line height is the theme's `tight` value;
  space headings with `Space` `gap`.
- `truncate` adds `overflow: hidden`, an ellipsis, `white-space: nowrap` and
  `min-width: 0` and `max-width: 100%`, so a truncated Heading clips inside an
  `Space` with any `align`.
- Every other HTML attribute (`id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event handlers) passes
  through. There is no `style` prop and no `as` prop.
- Override with `className` at `'&&'` specificity, never `!important`.

## Do / don't

- Do keep the outline in order: `h1`, then `h2`, then `h3`.
- Do override `size` and `weight` for a different look at the same level.
- Do put `truncate` on the Heading itself, not on a wrapper.
- Don't pick a level to get a size; set `size`.
- Don't use `Heading` for body text; use `Text`.
- Don't add margins to space headings; use `Space`.

modules.title: Text
modules.description: A run of text with themed size, tone and weight; unset props inherit from the surrounding text.
modules.importLine: import { Text, type TextProps } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A run of text with themed size, tone and weight. Use it to set text style by
prop instead of a style file: a body line, a meta line, a caption, an inline
error.

**Unset props inherit.** A bare `<Text>` adds no size, tone or weight, so it
looks exactly like the text around it. This keeps the look inside a `Chip`, a
`Button` or an error block: set only what you want to change.

Use something else for: a heading (`Heading`), a single chip (`Chip`), a line
of small metadata (`MetaLine`), a boxed alert (`Alert`).

## Usage

### Behaviour

- `tone` is not `Chip`'s `ChipTone` union. `primary` to `description` map to the
  theme's `color.text.*`; `danger` and `success` use the chip text colours.
- `danger` and `success` are for inline error and confirmation text. For a
  boxed message use `Alert`.
- `truncate` adds `overflow: hidden`, an ellipsis, `white-space: nowrap`,
  `min-width: 0` and `max-width: 100%`, so a truncated Text clips inside an
  `Space` with any `align`, and a `Space` nested in a row shrinks too (its
  root has `min-width: 0`).
- On `span`, `strong`, `em` and `label`, `truncate` also makes the element
  `inline-block`, because inline elements ignore overflow. `p` and `div` keep their block display.
- `as="p"` has its margin reset to 0; space paragraphs with `Space` `gap`.
- Every other HTML attribute (`id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event handlers) passes
  through. There is no `style` prop.
- Override with `className` at `'&&'` specificity, never `!important`.

## Do / don't

- Do set only the props you need; leave the rest to inherit.
- Do use the recipes: body `<Text>`, meta `size="sm" tone="muted"`, caption
  `size="xs" tone="faint"`.
- Do put `truncate` on the Text itself, not on a wrapper.
- Don't use `Text` for headings; use `Heading`.
- Don't set `tone="danger"` to build a box; it only colours text.
- Don't add margins to space text; use `Space`.

modules.title: Button
modules.description: A clickable action with a visual variant, optional icons, and a loading state.
modules.importLine: import { Button, type ButtonProps, type ButtonRadiusValue, type ButtonTypeValue } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A clickable action with a visual variant, optional icons, and a loading state.
Renders a `<div role="button">` (keyboard: Enter and Space, which it
preventDefaults, so Space does not scroll the page) unless `submit` is
set, in which case it renders a native `<button type="submit">`.

Use something else for: navigating back (`BackButton`), page-level actions in
the header (`PageActionsBar`, `PageActionsMenu`), sticky footer actions
(`PageFooterActions`), picking one of several options (`SegmentedControl`).

Every button but `link` is 32px tall: it pins its own line-height, so a
parent's (a Modal's 1.3) does not stretch it, and an icon-only button matches
a text one. Keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`) on `text` and `link` draws a solid
`border.focus` ring, since they have no border or fill of their own.

## Usage

### Choosing a variant

- `primary`: the one main action of a card, modal, or page (Save, Confirm).
- `default`: secondary actions; bordered.
- `text`: Cancel in a modal footer.
- `link`: inline row actions (Remove, Load more). It has no padding, so `radius`
  doesn't matter for it.
- `dashed`: an "add a row" affordance (as in `FieldList`).
- Add `danger` for destructive actions (Delete, Log out), on `primary` in a
  confirm or on `default` otherwise.
- To show an action is done (Copy turning into Copied!), change the label and
  add a `CheckIcon` prefix; there is no green button.

### Corners

The radius follows where the button sits (16px on a page, 8px in a `Card` or
`Modal`, 4px in a `Popover` or nested Card), so pass no `radius`; see
[corners](../corners.md). Pass it only to override.

### Submitting a form

`submit` renders a native submit button and `onClick` is then ignored: handle
the form's `action` or `onSubmit`. For a button outside its form (a `Card`
footer), pass the form's id as `form`. While the form action is pending the
button shows its spinner by itself.

## Do / don't

- Don't set `radius` to match the surface; it follows depth. Pass it only to
  override.
- Do give repeated row actions a distinguishing `ariaLabel` ("Remove Kindle").
- Don't pass `type="submit"`: it is not a valid variant. Use `submit`.
- Don't pass `onClick` to a submit button and expect it to run.
- Don't pass an element to `prefix`/`suffix` (`prefix={<SearchIcon />}`); pass
  the component.
- Don't wrap Button in a `<button>` or `<a>`: it is already interactive.

import { Button } from '@korzun/design/control';
import { useState } from 'react';

export default function Variants() {
  const [pressed, setPressed] = useState('nothing yet');
  return (
    <Space direction="vertical" align="start">
      <Space wrap>
        <Button type="primary" onClick={() => setPressed('Primary')}>
          Primary
        </Button>
        <Button onClick={() => setPressed('Default')}>Default</Button>
        <Button type="text" onClick={() => setPressed('Text')}>
          Text
        </Button>
        <Button type="link" onClick={() => setPressed('Link')}>
          Link
        </Button>
        <Button type="dashed" onClick={() => setPressed('Dashed')}>
          Dashed
        </Button>
      </Space>
      <Space wrap>
        <Button danger onClick={() => setPressed('Danger')}>
          Danger
        </Button>
        <Button type="primary" danger onClick={() => setPressed('Primary danger')}>
          Primary danger
        </Button>
      </Space>
      <Text tone="muted">Pressed: {pressed}</Text>
    </Space>
  );
}

changelog.text: **Breaking:** the `success` prop is removed. It only tinted a `default` button green (a `primary` one stayed blue), which read as a fourth kind of button. For a done state such as Copy turning into Copied!, change the label and add a `CheckIcon` prefix. The `color.bg.success` and `color.border.success` tokens stay. The Button examples now show every type, and `danger` on both `default` and `primary`.

A `link` button's spinner and `prefix`/`suffix` icons sit 0.5em from the label and centred on the text, like the other types; before they touched the label and sat high on the baseline. An icon-only link gets no extra space.
`text` and `link` buttons show a solid 2px `border.focus` ring on keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`); before they showed nothing. Mouse clicks still leave no ring.

Height no longer follows an inherited line-height: Buttons in a Dialog footer are 32px, not 35px, and an icon-only Button is 32px (was 31px, sitting 1px low) beside text Buttons. The label's line-height is pinned to 14px; `link` stays text-sized.

Surface depth: corners are concentric site-wide with no radius props. `Page` provides depth 0, `Dialog` 1, and `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` each provide one level deeper than where they sit; `Popover` (so `Menu` and the `Select` list) provides a fixed 2. Depth 0 is `radius.lg`, 1 is `md`, 2 and deeper is `sm`. `Button`, `Select`, `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` follow it; an explicit `Button radius` or `Select surface` still wins. With no `Page`, `Dialog`, `Card`, `CardRow`, `Alert` or `Surface` above it, a component keeps its 0.4.0 look; a bare `Card` (no `Page`) still counts as depth 0 and gives its contents depth 1, so its Buttons and nested Cards change as below.

**Visible changes:**
  - Buttons in a Card default to 8px (they were 16px unless `radius="card"` was set), and Buttons in a Dialog body are 8px.
  - Selects directly on a Page get the page look (16px and the card shadow); in a Card or Dialog they stay 8px. This includes Selects in your own boxes on a Page (a `useModalDialog` modal, a `recipe.card.shell` or `recipe.row` box), because depth cannot see hand-drawn boxes: wrap their contents in `Surface`, or pass `surface="card"`.
  - Without a Page, a bare `Card` counts as depth 0: its Buttons go from 16px to 8px, a Card nested in it steps down, and a `CardRow` in it is 8px.
  - A Card nested in a Card or Dialog steps down (8px, then 4px), and so do its Buttons and Selects; `size="small"` keeps its extra 1px.
  - `CardRow` is 16px on a Page and 8px inside a Card (it was always 16px).
  - Buttons and Selects inside a Popover or Menu are 4px.
The internal `ButtonRadiusContext` is removed; Dialog footer Buttons are unchanged (8px).

`Button` takes a `ref` and `ariaHasPopup`. Its interactive `<div role="button">` now defaults to `tabIndex={0}` so it is reachable by keyboard (`-1` when disabled or loading; an explicit `tabIndex` wins). Its keydown now calls `preventDefault()` on Enter and Space, so Space no longer scrolls the page and Enter opening a menu does not also activate its first item.

Buttons in a `Dialog` footer default to `radius="modal"`; an explicit `radius` still wins. The radius applies to the footer only (a Dialog nested in a footer is unaffected), and `footer={false}`, `''` and `null` render no footer bar.

modules.title: ChipsInput
modules.description: A tag field: the values show as coloured chips in an input box, typing filters a suggestion dropdown, and Enter adds a chip.
modules.importLine: import { ChipsInput, type ChipsInputProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A tag field: the current values render as coloured chips inside an input box,
typing filters a suggestion dropdown (a `Popover`), and Enter adds a chip. Fully
controlled: you own the `string[]`.

Use something else for: one value from a list (`Select`), one of a few fixed
options (`SegmentedControl`), free text (`TextInput`).

## Usage

### Keyboard

- ArrowDown / ArrowUp move the highlight; Enter or Tab adds the highlighted
  suggestion, else (with `allowCustom`) the trimmed typed text.
- **Tab with text typed adds a chip and keeps focus in the field** (it calls
  `preventDefault`); Tab on an empty field moves focus normally.
- Enter never submits the surrounding form while text is typed, even when
  nothing could be added.
- Backspace on an empty field removes the last chip.
- A value that matches an existing chip case-insensitively is not added.

### Styling

No `className`. The label is linked to the input with a generated id.

## Do / don't

- Do set `layout="horizontal"` and `dense` when it sits among other form fields
  in a `Card`; otherwise the label silently disappears.
- Do pick a `tone` that matches how the same values are tagged elsewhere.
- Do use it inside a `Modal`: the dropdown opens inside the open dialog, so it
  is not hidden behind it (see [popover](popover.md)).
- Don't rely on `name` for form submission.

changelog.text: **Breaking:** `chipColor` is renamed `tone` and takes a `ChipTone`, as `Chip` does; the `ChipColor` type is removed (use `ChipTone` from `@korzun/design/component`).
A `disabled` field hides its chips' remove (×) buttons instead of showing them dimmed, so the chips read as plain values.

The text field shares a line with the chips whenever 8rem is free. Before, it sized from an input's natural width (about 20 characters, ~200px at the 16px phone size) and dropped to its own empty line, making the box a line taller than its chips need.

Corners follow surface depth, like `Button` and `Select`: `lg` directly on a `Page`, `md` in a Card or Dialog (unchanged), `sm` two or more levels in (a nested Card, a `CardRow` or `Surface` in a Card, a Popover). A field's shaded row and the field in it take the same radius; `ChipsInput` chips and a horizontal `Switch`'s `inset` track are a step squarer than their box. With no surface above, each keeps its 0.6.0 look. **Visible changes:** fields and Tags placed directly on a Page get 16px corners, and Tags inside a `CardRow` in a Card get 4px. A text field, `ChipsInput` box or field label directly on a Page also moves its text 16px in from the edge (8px elsewhere), the inset `Button` keeps, so it clears the deeper corner.

`color.chip.neutral` text is a step stronger, so a neutral Tag or chip holds 4.5:1 on its tint over `bg.page`, `bg.card` and `bg.cardHeader`: light `#5E5E5E` (was `#6E6E6E`, 4.0:1 over `cardHeader`), dark `#A8ADB6`, the mode's `text.description` (was `#9CA1AB`, 4.47:1 over `page`). Fill and border are unchanged.
`Popover` renders inside an open `<dialog>` that contains its anchor, so `Select` and `ChipsInput` work in modals.

`Popover`:
  - `side` (`bottom`/`top`) and `align` (`start`/`center`/`end`).
  - Flips when the preferred side has no room.
  - Stays inside the viewport horizontally, unless `matchWidth` (then it lines up with the anchor exactly).
  - On the top side it is anchored by its bottom edge, and it re-measures when its content resizes (`ResizeObserver`), so it stays attached as content grows or shrinks.
  - The provisional first render is transparent rather than hidden, so an `autoFocus` child takes focus.
  - Exposes `data-side`.
  - Escape calls `onClose` unless already handled, without closing a surrounding dialog.
  - Defaults keep the same position when there is room below; `Select` and `ChipsInput` now open upward near the bottom of the viewport.

modules.title: DateTimeInput
modules.description: A date with an optional time, edited through the browser's native pickers and stored as an ISO 8601 string.
modules.importLine: import { DateTimeInput, type DateTimeInputProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A date with an optional time, edited through the browser's native date and time
pickers and stored as an ISO 8601 string. The time box stays disabled until
there is a date; clearing the date clears the time.

Use something else for: free text (`TextInput`), a year-only number
(`NumberInput`).

## Usage

### Behaviour

No `className`, no `disabled`, no `min` / `max`.

### Value format

| User has | `onChange` receives |
|---|---|
| no date | `undefined` |
| a date only | `'2023-06-06'` |
| date and time | `'2023-06-06T16:30:00Z'` |

- **The time is UTC, not local.** A stored `2015-08-04T22:30:00-05:00` displays
  as 2015-08-05, 03:30, and the user picks times in UTC too.
- Year and year-month values display as the 1st of the period (`1965` shows
  1965-01-01). Merely displaying doesn't rewrite them; editing does.
- An unreadable value (`'June 2023'`, `'2023-13-45'`) displays as empty.
- Native form data holds the date and the time as **two separate fields**
  (`name`, `nameTime`), not the composed value. Submit `value` from state.

## Do / don't

- Do keep the composed string from `onChange` in state and send that.
- Do tell users times are UTC if that matters for the field.
- Don't read `FormData.get(name)` expecting a timestamp; it is only the date part.

modules.title: FieldList
modules.description: An editable list of rows of text and number inputs, each with a remove button, plus an add button.
modules.importLine: import { FieldList, type ColumnDescriptor, type FieldListProps, type FieldRow } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
An editable list of rows, each with one or more text/number inputs and a
remove button, plus a dashed "add" button underneath. Fully controlled: you own
the rows and apply every change. On phones a row's columns stack.

Use something else for: a list of single words or tags (`ChipsInput`), a fixed
set of fields (`TextInput` / `NumberInput` directly).

## Usage

### Columns

A text column renders a `TextInput`, a number column a `NumberInput` (see
those docs for the controlled-ish behaviour). A number column shows a row value
only if it is a `number`; a numeric string displays as empty.

### Corners

The add button follows surface depth: 16px directly on a Page, 8px in a Card
or Modal, 4px deeper (8px with no Page, Modal, Card, CardRow, Alert or Surface above it).

### Behaviour to know

- The add button is 8px outside any surface and follows surface depth inside
  one (a Card body, a Modal, a Popover).
- Inputs have no labels; use `placeholder` to say what each column is.
- Every remove button is titled "Remove row" (its accessible name); they are not
  distinguished per row.
- No `className`.

## Do / don't

- Do generate `_key` once per row (`crypto.randomUUID()`), never from the index.
- Do strip `_key` before sending rows to the server.
- Don't store numeric columns as strings; they won't display.

modules.title: NumberInput
modules.description: A single-line field that reports a number, with a label and validation.
modules.importLine: import { NumberInput, type NumberInputProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A single-line field for a number, with an optional label and validation. It
parses with `parseFloat` and reports `number | undefined`. Same label/layout
system as `TextInput`.

Use something else for: one of a few fixed numbers (`SegmentedControl` or
`Select`), free text (`TextInput`).

## Usage

### Behaviour to know

- It is a plain `<input>` (no `type="number"`, no `inputMode`), so phones show
  the full text keyboard and there are no spinner arrows.
- The default check accepts text that both `Number()` and `parseFloat` read as a
  number: `1.5`, `-3`, `1e3` (reported as `1000`). `onChange` sends `parseFloat`
  of the text, so `0x10` passes but is reported as `0`.
- Invalid text stays visible with a red label and border; your state keeps the
  last valid number.

### What it has no prop for

No `className`, no `disabled`, no `min` / `max` / `step`.

## Do / don't

- Do pass `label={undefined}` explicitly when there is no visible label, and name the field with `ariaLabel`.
- Do report `onValidChange` into the form and disable submit while any field is invalid.
- Don't expect integer-only input unless your `validate` enforces it.

as 0. Other text turns the
label and border red, `onValidChange` fires once, and `onChange` is not called,
so the saved number stays at the last valid one. Type `abc` to see it.

modules.title: SegmentedControl
modules.description: A row of equal-width radio segments in a track, with a lens that slides to the checked one.
modules.importLine: import { SegmentedControl, type SegmentedControlProps, type SegmentedOption } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A row of equal-width radio segments in a track, with a lens that slides to the
checked one. Options can be text, or an icon over a small caption. Optionally
clearable, and read-only when `onChange` is omitted. Generic over the value
type: `V extends string`.

Use something else for: many options or long labels (`Select`), on/off
(`Switch`), actions (`Button`).

## Usage

### Behaviour

No `className`, no `name` (not a form field). Type options with the exported
`SegmentedOption<V>` (and props with `SegmentedControlProps<V>`).

### Keyboard

On the group: ArrowRight/ArrowUp and ArrowLeft/ArrowDown step one option and do
not wrap; Home/End jump to the ends; digits 1–9 pick that option; Backspace and
Delete clear when `clearable`. Modified keys (Ctrl/Cmd/Alt) are left alone.

### Choosing a surface

The track and lens take the radius of the surface depth they sit at (see
[corners](../corners.md)): `md` in a card or modal, `lg` directly on a `Page`,
`sm` two or more levels in.

- Directly in a `Card` body: omit `surface` (`'card'`).
- Inside a shaded `bg.cardHeader` row you built (label left, control right):
  `surface="row"`, so the row itself is the track and the lens is flush with it.

## Do / don't

- Do keep it to a handful of short options; segments are equal columns.
- Do pass `clearable` whenever `null` is a valid answer, or the user can never
  get back to it.
- Don't pass `onChange={() => {}}` to show a value; omit `onChange` for read-only.

are typed to the option values. The `label` names the group for assistive tech
and is not drawn, so put a visible label beside the control yourself.

Omit `onChange` to show a value without letting it change: the segments are
marked `aria-disabled` and ignore clicks and keys. A `null` value checks
nothing and draws no lens.

In a Card body the control paints its own track. In the shaded Card header the
header is the track, so `surface="row"` paints nothing and only the lens
shows. The corner is the same in both: the control belongs inside a card or
modal.

modules.title: Select
modules.description: A single-value dropdown with type-to-search, an optional "Add: …" entry for new values, a clear button, and a loading state.
modules.importLine: import { Select, type SelectOption, type SelectProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A single-value dropdown with type-to-search (on by default), an optional "Add:
…" entry for new values, a clear button, and a loading state. The dropdown is a
`Popover`, so it escapes clipping cards. Its list is drawn like a `Menu`: a
4px inset pad, `sm`-rounded 14px options, the `cardStack` shadow, `bg.hover` on
hover and `brand.light` on the keyboard-highlighted option.

Use something else for: 2–5 options that fit in one row (`SegmentedControl`),
several values (`ChipsInput`), on/off (`Switch`).

## Usage

### Choosing a surface

Follow [corners](../corners.md):

- Usually omit it: the default follows where the select sits. Directly on a
  `Page` it is `'page'`; in a card or dialog (and outside any surface) it is
  `'card'`; two or more surfaces deep it is `'inset'`.
- `'card'`: `radius.md`, no shadow.
- `'page'`: `radius.lg` + `shadow.cardStack`, like a card.
- `'inset'`: `radius.sm`, no shadow, for a select nested inside an inset box.
- Pass `surface` only to override the depth.

### Forms

There is no hidden input carrying `value`: native `FormData` will not contain
the selection (only the search text while open). Keep `value` in state and
submit that. The `<label>` targets the search box, so it is not the closed
trigger's accessible name; the trigger announces the selected label or
placeholder.

### Keyboard

Closed: Enter, Space or ArrowDown open it. Open: ArrowUp/ArrowDown move (and
wrap), Enter selects, Escape or Tab close. The highlight starts on the first
option, not the current value.

### Inside a dialog

It works inside a `Modal` or a modal `<dialog>`: the list opens inside the
open dialog (see [popover](popover.md)).

### Styling

No `className`.

## Do / don't

- Do pass `clearable={false}` when an empty value is invalid.
- Don't pass `surface="page"` inside a card; let the depth decide.

A controlled single-value picker. Opening it swaps the trigger for a search

start open.

`horizontal` puts the label and trigger in one card-header row, `vertical`
stacks the label above the trigger in that row, and `inline` is just the
trigger with the label beside it.

`allowCreate` adds an "Add: …" entry when what you type matches no label

A set value shows a ✕ that sends `undefined` to `onChange`. Pass

`loading` shows a spinner and "Loading…" in place of the value, and the select
