changelog.text: The option list matches `Menu`: a 4px inset pad, 4px-rounded options with a 2px gap, 14px text (was 12.8px), the flat `cardStack` shadow (was `hoverLift`) and `bg.hover` on hover (was `bg.cardHeader`). The keyboard highlight is unchanged.

Dark `color.border.light` is `#333439` (was `#2B2C30`, 1.10:1 on `bg.page` and 1.23:1 on `bg.card`, so hairline rules all but vanished); it is now 1.24:1 and 1.39:1, at or above light mode's step. A loading `Select`'s border in dark is a shade lighter. Light is unchanged.

Surface depth: corners are concentric site-wide with no radius props. `Page` provides depth 0, `Dialog` 1, and `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` each provide one level deeper than where they sit; `Popover` (so `Menu` and the `Select` list) provides a fixed 2. Depth 0 is `radius.lg`, 1 is `md`, 2 and deeper is `sm`. `Button`, `Select`, `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` follow it; an explicit `Button radius` or `Select surface` still wins. With no `Page`, `Dialog`, `Card`, `CardRow`, `Alert` or `Surface` above it, a component keeps its 0.4.0 look; a bare `Card` (no `Page`) still counts as depth 0 and gives its contents depth 1, so its Buttons and nested Cards change as below.

**Visible changes:**
  - Buttons in a Card default to 8px (they were 16px unless `radius="card"` was set), and Buttons in a Dialog body are 8px.
  - Selects directly on a Page get the page look (16px and the card shadow); in a Card or Dialog they stay 8px. This includes Selects in your own boxes on a Page (a `useModalDialog` modal, a `recipe.card.shell` or `recipe.row` box), because depth cannot see hand-drawn boxes: wrap their contents in `Surface`, or pass `surface="card"`.
  - Without a Page, a bare `Card` counts as depth 0: its Buttons go from 16px to 8px, a Card nested in it steps down, and a `CardRow` in it is 8px.
  - A Card nested in a Card or Dialog steps down (8px, then 4px), and so do its Buttons and Selects; `size="small"` keeps its extra 1px.
  - `CardRow` is 16px on a Page and 8px inside a Card (it was always 16px).
  - Buttons and Selects inside a Popover or Menu are 4px.
`Select` `surface` gains `'inset'` (`radius.sm`, no shadow), used two or more levels deep.
`Popover` renders inside an open `<dialog>` that contains its anchor, so `Select` and `ChipsInput` work in modals.

`Popover`:
  - `side` (`bottom`/`top`) and `align` (`start`/`center`/`end`).
  - Flips when the preferred side has no room.
  - Stays inside the viewport horizontally, unless `matchWidth` (then it lines up with the anchor exactly).
  - On the top side it is anchored by its bottom edge, and it re-measures when its content resizes (`ResizeObserver`), so it stays attached as content grows or shrinks.
  - The provisional first render is transparent rather than hidden, so an `autoFocus` child takes focus.
  - Exposes `data-side`.
  - Escape calls `onClose` unless already handled, without closing a surrounding dialog.
  - Defaults keep the same position when there is room below; `Select` and `ChipsInput` now open upward near the bottom of the viewport.

modules.title: Switch
modules.description: An on/off toggle with an optional label and description, a full-row layout for forms, and a loading state for saves in flight.
modules.importLine: import { Switch, type SwitchProps, type SwitchRadiusValue } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
An on/off toggle (`role="switch"`) with an optional label and description, a
full-row `horizontal` layout for forms, and a `loading` state for saves in
flight. Controlled: you own `checked`. The unchecked track is `bg.switchOff`, a
mid-grey that holds 3:1 on the page, a card and a shaded row in both themes.

Use something else for: one of several options (`SegmentedControl`, `Select`),
an action that happens on click (`Button`).

## Usage

### Behaviour

No `className`. Keyboard: Enter and Space toggle. Clicks and those keys stop
propagation, so a switch inside a clickable card row won't trigger the row.

### Choosing a radius

See [corners](../corners.md).

- In a shaded row (`layout="horizontal"`, or inside any field row): omit it
  (`inset`, a track one radius step squarer than the row: 4px in a Card's 8px
  row, 8px in a Page's 16px row).
- In a `Card` header (`headerAction`), or anywhere with no nearby corner to
  echo: `radius="pill"`.

## Do / don't

- Do pass `loading` while the save runs instead of `disabled`; `disabled` means
  "you may not change this".
- Do give a label-less switch an `ariaLabel`; `name` is a machine key.
- Don't expect a switch to submit with a `<form>`; send `checked` from state.
- Don't put an interactive element in `description` of a `horizontal` switch:
  clicking it toggles the switch.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description:
A controlled switch with a visible `label`. `onChange` receives the new
value, not an event; Enter and Space toggle it from the keyboard.

examples.title: Layouts
examples.description:
`default` puts the track and the label inline. `horizontal` is a full-width
shaded row with the label and `description` on the left and the track on the
right, and the whole row toggles. In both, the `description` is helper text
linked by `aria-describedby`.

examples.title: Radius
examples.description:
`inset` is the track corner for a switch in a shaded row: concentric with the
row's own corner. `pill` is the capsule for a switch with no nearby corner to
echo.

examples.title: In a Card
examples.description:
A setting row in the body takes the default `inset` track. A switch in the
header, with no nearby corner, takes `radius="pill"`; with no visible label it
needs an `ariaLabel`.

examples.title: Loading and disabled
examples.description:
`loading` marks a save in flight: clicks are ignored and the thumb turns into
a loading mark after a short delay (a squared ring on the default `inset` radius,
a round spinner on `pill`), while the switch keeps its colour. `disabled`
fades the whole control and means "you may not change this". The button holds
the save open; the count shows that clicks during it do nothing.

modules.body:
A multi-line text field with an optional label, validation, an optional
auto-grow mode, and a character counter near `maxLength`. Same label/layout
system as `TextInput`.

Use something else for: single-line text (`TextInput`), tags (`ChipsInput`).

## Usage

### Styling

No `className`, no `disabled`, no `rows`, never resizable by the user
(`resize: none`).

## Do / don't

- Do use `autoResize` for long free text so the card doesn't scroll inside itself.
- Do set `maxLength` when the server has a limit; the counter only appears near it.
- Do set `ariaLabel` on a textarea with no visible `label`.
- Don't expect `onChange('')`; an empty field reports `undefined`.
- Don't try to shrink it below 7rem / 10rem with CSS; the min height is inline.

modules.title: TextInput

modules.importLine: import { TextInput, type TextInputAction, type TextInputProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A single-line text (or password) field with an optional label, optional
validation, and a character counter that appears near `maxLength`. The default
`horizontal` layout puts the label and field on one shaded row, which is how
form fields look inside a `Card`.

Use something else for: multi-line text (`TextArea`), numbers (`NumberInput`),
picking from a list (`Select`), a list of tags (`ChipsInput`), dates
(`DateTimeInput`).

## Usage

### Controlled-ish

The field keeps its own text. It re-syncs from `value` only when the `value`
prop changes. While `validate` fails, the field shows the invalid text but
`onChange` is not called, so your state keeps the last valid value. Track
`onValidChange` to block submit.

### Icons inside the field

`prefix` draws a decorative icon at the field's left end (`prefix={SearchIcon}`),
in `text.muted`; the text moves clear of it. It is hidden from screen readers
and lets clicks through to the field. `action` puts an icon button at the right
end. Together they make a search box: a search icon, and a clear button shown
only while there is text.

### What it has no prop for

No `className`, no `disabled`, no `id`.

## Do / don't

- Do keep the default `horizontal` layout for fields in a `Card` body; use
  `vertical` when the label is long or the field is wide.
- Do coalesce `undefined` (`v ?? ''`) if your state is a plain string.
- Do give an `action` an `ariaLabel`; the icon alone has no name.
- Do name a field with a `prefix` by `label` or `ariaLabel`; the icon says nothing to a screen reader.
- Don't use `prefix` for something clickable; use `action`.
- Do set `ariaLabel` on a field with no visible `label`.

modules.title: ConfirmModal
modules.description: A ready-made yes/no modal with a title, a body, and Cancel and Confirm buttons.
modules.importLine: import { ConfirmModal, type ConfirmModalProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A ready-made yes/no modal built on [`Modal`](modal.md): a title, a body
(`children`), and a footer with a text Cancel and a primary Confirm button. It
is always mounted and fully controlled by `isOpen`.

Use something else for: a modal with its own form or more than two actions
(use [`Modal`](modal.md) for anything that is not yes/no), or a non-blocking
notice (toast).

## Usage

### Behaviour to know

- Footer buttons already get `md` corners from `Modal`'s depth; the dialog uses
  `recipe.modal.dialog` (`radius.lg`, it sits on the page). See
  [corners](../corners.md).
- `onCancel` is the single dismissal path, so whatever you do there runs for
  Escape and backdrop clicks too.

### Styling

No `className`.

## Do / don't

- Do pass `loading` while the request runs, so the user can't dismiss mid-flight.
- Do close the modal in both `onCancel` and (after success) `onConfirm`.
- Don't render it conditionally (`{open && <ConfirmModal …/>}`); toggle `isOpen`.
- Don't pass `icon={<AlertOctagonIcon />}`; pass the component.

click on the backdrop. This demo starts open; Sync library opens it again.

modules.title: Menu
modules.description: A button that opens a list of actions and links, described as data, with keyboard handling built in.
modules.importLine: import { Menu, type MenuActionItem, type MenuIntentProps, type MenuItem, type MenuLinkItem, type MenuProps, type MenuTriggerProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A button that opens a list of actions and links, described as data, with keyboard
handling built in. It follows the WAI-ARIA menu button pattern. You render the
trigger; Menu gives it the props it needs, draws the
list in a [`Popover`](popover.md) anchored to it, and handles focus and the
keyboard. Pass the items in `items`. There are no child
components and no style file to write.

[`PageActionsBar`](page-actions-bar.md) and [`PageActionsMenu`](page-actions-menu.md)
are built on Menu.

Use something else for: choosing a value ([`Select`](select.md)), page-header
actions ([`PageActionsBar`](page-actions-bar.md) on desktop,
[`PageActionsMenu`](page-actions-menu.md) on mobile).

## Usage

### The trigger

`MenuTriggerProps` is `{ ref, onClick, ariaExpanded, ariaControls, ariaHasPopup: 'menu' }`,
shaped for [`Button`](button.md), so `{...p}` needs no glue. `ref` is a
callback ref (`(node: HTMLElement | null) => void`), so it attaches to any
element without a cast. `ariaControls` is the menu's id while open and
`undefined` while closed. For any other element, pass `ref={p.ref}`, call
`onClick` on click, and map the rest to `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and
`aria-haspopup`; the "Other triggers" example shows it.

### Items

An item is either an action or a link. TypeScript rejects an item with both
`onClick` and `to`, or with neither. Every item takes `label`, `Icon`, `danger`,
`disabled`, `separatorBefore` and `intentProps`; actions add `onClick`, links add
`to`. The tables under Props list each field.

### Keyboard

| Key                                  | Does                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Click, Enter or Space on the trigger | Opens the menu and focuses the first enabled item.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Down / Up                            | Next / previous enabled item, wrapping.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Home / End                           | First / last enabled item.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Enter, Space (or a click)            | Activates the item: the menu closes, focus returns to the trigger, then the action runs or the link navigates.                                                                                                           |
| Escape                               | Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Tab / Shift+Tab                      | Closes the menu; focus moves to the tabbable element after / before the trigger, skipping inert and hidden ones. Inside an open `<dialog>` it stays within the dialog; with nothing there, focus returns to the trigger. |
| Pointer-down outside                 | Closes the menu without moving focus.                                                                                                                                                                                    |

### Behaviour to know

- Escape and outside presses go to the innermost open layer first: a Select
  list opened over the menu closes before it, and a Menu inside a
  [`Modal`](modal.md) closes before the Modal.
- Opening another Menu closes the first (the press on its trigger is outside).
- If the focused item disappears while the menu is open, focus moves to the
  first enabled item. With every item disabled, the menu itself takes focus.
- The menu sits `space.sm` from the trigger and portals out of clipping
  ancestors (into an open `<dialog>` when inside one).

## Do / don't

- Do use Menu for any list of actions or links behind a button.
- Do pass icon components (`Icon: BookIcon`), not elements.
- Don't hand-build `role="menu"`, or wire a Popover and buttons yourself.
- Don't wrap the trigger in another `<button>`; spread the props onto it.
- Don't use a Menu to pick a value that stays shown; that is a `Select`.

changelog.text: Surface depth: corners are concentric site-wide with no radius props. `Page` provides depth 0, `Dialog` 1, and `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` each provide one level deeper than where they sit; `Popover` (so `Menu` and the `Select` list) provides a fixed 2. Depth 0 is `radius.lg`, 1 is `md`, 2 and deeper is `sm`. `Button`, `Select`, `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` follow it; an explicit `Button radius` or `Select surface` still wins. With no `Page`, `Dialog`, `Card`, `CardRow`, `Alert` or `Surface` above it, a component keeps its 0.4.0 look; a bare `Card` (no `Page`) still counts as depth 0 and gives its contents depth 1, so its Buttons and nested Cards change as below.

**Visible changes:**
  - Buttons in a Card default to 8px (they were 16px unless `radius="card"` was set), and Buttons in a Dialog body are 8px.
  - Selects directly on a Page get the page look (16px and the card shadow); in a Card or Dialog they stay 8px. This includes Selects in your own boxes on a Page (a `useModalDialog` modal, a `recipe.card.shell` or `recipe.row` box), because depth cannot see hand-drawn boxes: wrap their contents in `Surface`, or pass `surface="card"`.
  - Without a Page, a bare `Card` counts as depth 0: its Buttons go from 16px to 8px, a Card nested in it steps down, and a `CardRow` in it is 8px.
  - A Card nested in a Card or Dialog steps down (8px, then 4px), and so do its Buttons and Selects; `size="small"` keeps its extra 1px.
  - `CardRow` is 16px on a Page and 8px inside a Card (it was always 16px).
  - Buttons and Selects inside a Popover or Menu are 4px.

`theme.space` values are typed as `SpaceValue` (`${number}rem`), so `gap={theme.space.sm}` on `Popover` and `Menu` needs no `as PopoverGap` cast. `Theme['space']` is now typed `${number}rem`, so hand-built Theme objects or mocks with `px` values stop type-checking.

New `Menu` (control): a button that opens a list of actions and links, described as an `items` array (`onClick` for actions, `to` for links; `Icon`, `danger`, `disabled`, `separatorBefore`, `intentProps`). Arrow keys, Home and End move between items, and Escape returns focus to the trigger. `surface` is `solid` or `glass`.

`Menu` trigger props: `ref` is a callback ref, so it attaches to a `<button>`, an `<a>` or a `Button` without a cast; `ariaControls` is set only while the menu is open. Tab from an open menu skips inert, hidden and `tabindex="-1"` elements and stays inside an open `<dialog>`. A disabled link item has no `href`.

`PageActionsMenu` and `PageActionsBar` are rebuilt on `Menu`: arrow keys, Home and End move between actions, and Escape returns focus to the trigger. `PageActionItem` is now `MenuActionItem & { primary?, align? }`: it gains an optional `Icon` (shown in the menus, ignored by the bar's primary Buttons), and `to` is not allowed.

modules.title: Modal
modules.description: A modal on a native dialog element with a title, a body and an optional footer of actions.
modules.importLine: import { Modal, type ModalProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A modal on a native `<dialog>` (via [`useModal`](use-modal.md)): a title, a body
(`children`), and an optional `footer` for actions. It is always mounted and
fully controlled by `open`. The title names the dialog for assistive tech.

Use something else for: a yes/no question ([`ConfirmModal`](confirm-modal.md)),
a non-blocking notice (toast).

## Usage

### Behaviour to know

- Escape and a backdrop press-and-release both call `onClose`; it is the
  single dismissal path. `canDismiss={false}` blocks both.
- Escape goes to the innermost open layer first: a `Select` list or other
  popover open inside the dialog closes before the dialog, and a dialog opened
  over a still-open popover closes before that popover.
- Always mounted: toggle `open`, don't render it conditionally.
- Focus is native: `showModal()` moves focus into the dialog and restores it
  on close.
- Clicks inside the dialog do not bubble to clickable ancestors.
- Content is one surface level in: Buttons in the body, header and `footer`
  (including nested ones inside a `Space`) default to 8px. An explicit
  `radius` on a Button still wins.

## Do / don't

- Do use [`ConfirmModal`](confirm-modal.md) for yes/no questions.
- Do pass `canDismiss={!loading}` while a request runs.
- Don't set `radius` on Buttons inside a Modal by hand; the depth does it.
- Don't write your own modal style files; build on `Modal`.
- Don't render it conditionally (`{open && <Modal …/>}`); toggle `open`.

modules.title: Popover
modules.description: A positioning primitive that shows content in a portal below or above an anchor element, and paints nothing itself.
modules.importLine: import { Popover, type PopoverAlign, type PopoverGap, type PopoverProps, type PopoverSide } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A positioning primitive: renders `children` in a portal on `document.body`,
`position: fixed` below or above an anchor element, so a dropdown can escape
ancestors that clip overflow (rounded cards). It paints **nothing** itself: no
background, border, shadow, or radius. `Menu`, `Select` and `ChipsInput` build
their dropdowns on it.

Use something else for: a modal (`Modal`), page action menus
(`PageActionsMenu`, `PageActionsBar`), choosing from a list (`Select`).

## Usage

### Behaviour to know

- **Content mounts one commit after `open` flips.** An effect keyed on `open`
  that reaches into the content must wait for it: use a ref callback or
  `autoFocus` instead.
- **Flip.** It opens on `side`. If the content does not fit on that side and
  the other side has more room, it opens on the other side. When neither side
  fits it keeps whichever has more room.
- **Clamp.** Only when `matchWidth` is false: `left` is clamped so the
  content stays `gap` pixels inside the viewport's left and right edges;
  content wider than the viewport pins to `gap`. With `matchWidth` it lines up
  with the anchor exactly, edge margin or not. There is no vertical clamp.
- **Align.** `align` sets the edge it lines up with: `start`, `center` or `end`. Use `end` for an anchor at the right edge of the screen, so the content grows leftwards.
- **Top side is anchored by its bottom edge** (CSS `bottom`), so a popover
  above its anchor stays attached when its content grows or shrinks.
- **`data-side`.** The wrapper carries `data-side="bottom"` or `"top"`: the side
  actually used after flipping. It also carries `data-preferred-side`, the
  `side` prop, so a flip can be told from a choice. Style against these (an
  arrow, an animation origin) rather than against the `side` prop.
- It re-measures, flip decision included, on window resize, on any scroll
  (capture phase), and when its content resizes (`ResizeObserver`, where the
  browser has it), so it stays attached to a scrolled anchor and to content
  that changes size.
- Its first render is transparent (`opacity: 0`) and is measured in a layout
  effect before paint, so it never flashes at 0,0 or on the wrong side. It is
  not `visibility: hidden`, so an `autoFocus` child takes focus on mount.
- **No focus management.** Focus stays where it was; return it yourself if
  closing should move it.
- z-index is `theme.zIndex.sticky` (1000). Inside an open `<dialog>` it portals
  into that dialog, so it shows in the top layer; this also matches a non-modal
  `show()` dialog. The target is resolved each time the popover opens, so it
  also works when it mounts already open.
- Clicking the anchor does not count as "outside", so a toggle button on the
  anchor works without racing `onClose`.

### Layers

Escape and outside pointer-down close the innermost open layer first. With
`onClose`, an open popover joins a layer stack shared with other popovers and
open `Modal`s, in the order they opened. A popover registers once its portal
target resolves, one commit after each opening, so a `Modal` that mounts
already open together with an already-open popover inside it still sits below
that popover.

- An Escape keydown anywhere in the document goes to the top layer only,
  unless the event is already `defaultPrevented` (a control such as
  `Select` handled it first). A popover on top calls `onClose` and
  `preventDefault()`s the key, so an enclosing native `<dialog>` does not
  also fire `cancel` and close. A `Modal` on top keeps the key: its own
  `cancel` closes it, and the popover beneath stays open.
- A mousedown closes every layer above the one it lands in (every layer,
  when it lands outside them all), top first. A press in a nested popover
  closes neither it nor its parent; a press inside a `Modal` opened over a
  popover does not close that popover.

### Styling the surface

Content is two surface levels in: Buttons and Selects inside a popover are 4px,
wherever the anchor sits.

A popover is a floating layer: corners `radius.md` with `shadow.hoverLift` (or
`recipe.glass`), and the items inside it `radius.sm`. See
[corners](../corners.md). The "Basic" example draws such a surface.

```ts
menu: {
  backgroundColor: theme.color.bg.card,
  border: `1px solid ${theme.color.border.strong}`,
  borderRadius: theme.radius.md,
  boxShadow: theme.shadow.hoverLift,
  padding: theme.space.xs,
},
item: { borderRadius: theme.radius.sm, padding: theme.space.md },
```

## Do / don't

- Do anchor to a `Button` through its `ref`, or wrap any element in a `<div ref>`.
- Do give the content its own surface and radius; the wrapper is transparent.
- Do call `preventDefault()` in your own Escape handler if you close the
  popover yourself, so `onClose` is not called a second time.
- Don't expect it to close on selection; that is your code.

modules.description: A small coloured chip for a category, status or value, optionally clickable.
modules.importLine: import { Chip, type ChipProps, type ChipTone } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A small coloured chip (an inline `<span>`) for a category, status, or value:
an author, a subject, "Read only". Optionally clickable, in which case it
becomes `role="button"` with `tabIndex=0` and Enter/Space.

Use something else for: an editable list of chips (`ChipsInput` in
`@korzun/design/control`), an action (`Button`), a count on a nav tab
(`NavItem.badge`).

## Usage

### Choosing a tone

`ChipTone` is `keyof Theme['color']['chip']`. There are two groups: label tones
are **domain names** (what kind of thing the tag names) and status tones are
**meanings** (what state it reports). Neither group is a set of colour names:
never pick a tone for its colour. Pick by what the tag *is*:

Status tones report a state:

| Tone | Use for |
|---|---|
| `success` | Something went well (Published, Paid). |
| `warning` | Needs attention soon (Overdue, Expiring). |
| `danger` | Something failed or is blocked (Failed, Rejected). |
| `info` | Neutral news (Scheduled, New). |
| `neutral` | A state with no category ("no change"): quiet grey. |

Label tones name a kind of thing:

| Tone | Use for |
|---|---|
| `status` | Legacy; kept for Bookplate's existing chips. Don't pick it for new state tags. |
| `author` | A person who wrote something. |
| `series` | A series name. |
| `subject` | A subject / genre / keyword. The default. |
| `book` | A book or title. |
| `entryType` | The kind of an entry or record. |
| `user` | An app user / account. |
| `rating` | A rating value. |

Note the name clash: `status` is a legacy label tone despite its name; for a state use `success`/`warning`/`danger`/`info`, or `neutral` when it carries no meaning.

Each tone has its own `text`, `bg`, and `border` in both light and dark themes.
A consumer's theme can't add tones; the list is fixed by the `Theme` type.

### Styling

No `className`, no `ariaLabel`.

### Corners

At both sizes the corners follow surface depth: `md` in a Card or modal, `lg`
directly on a `Page`, `sm` one more level in (a `CardRow` in a Card, a Popover);
see [corners](../corners.md).

## Do / don't

- Do choose `tone` by meaning, so the same kind of thing is the same colour
  everywhere.
- Do use `tone="warning"` for "Overdue".
- Do use `size="sm"` inside text rows and lists.
- Don't use `neutral` just to make a tag grey when it has a category.
- Don't use `subject` or `author` to mean warning or success.
- Don't use `info` to look like a link (it shares a hue with links; use
  `Button type="link"` for actions).
- Don't use `status` for a new state tag; it is a legacy label tone.
- Don't nest a clickable Chip inside another clickable element (Button, a
  clickable Card); both would fire.

modules.title: CodeBlock
modules.description: A block of code in mono type that scrolls or wraps, can show highlighted children, and can offer a Copy button.
modules.importLine: import { CodeBlock, type CodeBlockProps } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A block of code in mono type on a tinted box, for a command, an import line or a
snippet a reader may copy. It scrolls sideways (or wraps), shows either plain
text or highlighted children, and can add a Copy button.

Use something else for: a name or short expression inside a sentence (`Code`),
data in rows and columns (`Table`).

## Usage

### Plain and highlighted

Pass `code` alone for plain text. To colour it, pass highlighted spans as
`children`: they replace what shows, and Copy still copies `code`, so keep the
two the same text. Pass the inner `<code>` content (or its spans), not Shiki's whole
`<pre>`: `CodeBlock` renders its own `pre`.

### Code colours

`CodeBlock` sets these CSS variables on its root from `theme.color.code`, the
names Shiki's css-variables theme emits with `variablePrefix: '--code-'`. A
highlighter that uses that theme follows the light and dark themes with no
colour work.

| Variable | Theme token |
| --- | --- |
| `--code-foreground` | `color.code.foreground` |
| `--code-token-keyword` | `color.code.keyword` |
| `--code-token-string` | `color.code.string` |
| `--code-token-string-expression` | `color.code.string` |
| `--code-token-function` | `color.code.function` |
| `--code-token-parameter` | `color.code.parameter` |
| `--code-token-constant` | `color.code.constant` |
| `--code-token-punctuation` | `color.code.punctuation` |
| `--code-token-comment` | `color.code.comment` |
| `--code-token-link` | `color.code.link` |

Shiki's other variables (`--code-background`, `--code-token-inserted`,
`--code-token-deleted`, `--code-token-changed`, `--code-ansi-*`) are not set,
so those tokens fall back to the inherited colour. For highlighted HTML rendered
outside `CodeBlock`, such as markdown, spread `theme.recipe.codeColours` on its
wrapper to set the same ten variables.

### Copy

`copyable` adds a text button that reads Copy. Pressed, it writes `code` to the
clipboard and reads Copied with a check for 2 seconds; pressing again restarts
the 2 seconds. Where there is no clipboard (an insecure page) or the write is
refused, it reads Could not copy for 2 seconds and throws nothing. A visually
hidden status region announces the result. `copyLabel` is the idle button's
accessible name.

### Scrolling and wrapping

A long line scrolls inside the box and never widens the page; the right edge
fades while more is hidden, since phones hide scrollbars. `wrap` breaks long
lines instead.

### Styling

Takes `className` on the root, merged last. The look is fixed: it is the
`theme.recipe.codeBlock` look, drawn by the component.

### Corners

The box's corners follow where it sits: `lg` on a `Page`, `md` in a Card or
`Surface`, `sm` two levels in. The Copy button sits one level deeper. In dark
mode directly on a `Page` a 1px `border.default` edge separates the box from the
page. See [corners](../corners.md).

## Do / don't

- Do pass the same text as `code` and as the highlighted `children`.
- Don't use it inline in a sentence; use `Code`.

modules.title: MetaLine
modules.description: A short run of data about one record, as a dotted line or labelled pairs, wrapping between data, never inside one.
modules.importLine: import { MetaLine, type MetaLineItem, type MetaLinePair, type MetaLineProps } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A short run of data about one record. Two looks:

- **A separated line**, a row's secondary line: "Frank Herbert · Book 3 · 42%".
  Pass `separator`.
- **Labelled facts**, a card's body: "Format EPUB   Size 2.1 MB". Pass
  `{ label, value }` items and no separator; items are spaced by gaps.

Either way it wraps *between* data, never inside one.

Use something else for: many fields, or the same fields across records
(`Table`), a row's primary title (`Text` or `Heading`).

## Usage

### Items and pairs

`items` holds nodes and `{ label, value }` pairs, mixed freely. A pair shows
its label in `text.faint`, capitalized by CSS (`'cover fit'` shows as "Cover
Fit"), then its value.

- `null`, `undefined` and `false` items are skipped, and so is a pair whose
  `value` is one of them, so pass optional data as `cond && value` or
  `{ label, value: maybe }`.
- `''` and `0` are kept; filter them yourself.
- **Renders `null`** when every item is skipped: no empty line is left behind.
- Items are keyed by position.

### Separator

`separator` takes one character (`'·'`, `'|'`, `'/'`); `''` counts as unset. It sits in a 1em
cell before each item, drawn by CSS (`::before`), so screen readers read only
the data, and the one that would lead a line is clipped: none dangles at a line
end or starts the next line. It is drawn in `text.muted`. Without
`separator`, items are `space.lg` apart and lines `space.sm` apart.

One character means one grapheme (an emoji with a skin tone counts as one). A
longer string such as `' | '` or `'->'` overflows the 1em cell and overlaps the
next item, so in development MetaLine logs a `console.warn` once per such
separator. It works in right-to-left text too: the clip uses logical
properties, so the line start is clipped on whichever side it is.

### Long data

A datum never wraps inside itself. One wider than the whole line ellipsizes.

### Typography

MetaLine sets no font size or colour of its own except the label and
separator colours; wrap it in `Text` to set the rest (`size="sm"` in a card
body, `tone="faint"` for a row's secondary line).

## Do / don't

- Do pass conditional data as `cond && value`; `false` is skipped.
- Do set typography by wrapping the line in `Text` (`size`, `tone`); the items inherit it.
- Don't join data into one string with your own " · ": wrapping then breaks
  inside a datum and the dots are read aloud.
- Don't pass empty strings; with a separator they leave a stray one.

modules.title: Table
modules.description: A generic data table that scrolls in its own box on a wide screen and stacks each row, labelled, on a phone.
modules.importLine: import { Table, type TableColumn, type TableProps } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A generic data table: pass `columns` and `rows` and it draws a bordered box
with a header row and a row per item. On a wide screen it scrolls sideways
inside its own box when it is too wide; on a phone each row stacks, with every
value labelled by its column title.

Use something else for: a short list of items with actions (`CardRow`), a
list of name and value pairs (`MetaLine`), a layout grid (`Space`). A table is for data with the same fields in every row.

## Usage

### Columns and rows

Each column has a `key` and a `title`. By default a cell shows the row's field
named by `key`; `render(row, index)` draws it instead, for a `Chip` or a
`Button`. A missing value (`null` or `undefined`) shows a dash; `0`, `false`
and `''` show as themselves. Type the table with its row type
(`<Table<Book> … />`) to check `render` and `rowKey`.

### `rowKey`

Name the field that identifies a row (`rowKey="id"`), or pass a function that
returns a unique string (`rowKey={(row, i) => row.isbn}`). It must be unique
and stable, as a React key is.

### Phone layout, `label` and `wide`

Below the mobile breakpoint the header is hidden for sighted users and each
row becomes a block: short cells share a line, each prefixed by its column
`title` and a colon. `label` renames that prefix, and `label: false` shows the
value bare (for a button). `wide: true` gives a cell the full width of the
stacked row, for a long description. Pass `ariaLabel` to name the table for
screen readers.

### Empty

With no rows the header stays. `empty` fills one row across all columns; omit
it and the table shows the header only.

### Scrolling and `minWidth`

The table never widens the page: it scrolls inside its box. `minWidth`
(`'40rem'`) keeps columns readable by making the table that wide on a wide
screen before it scrolls. A phone ignores it, because rows stack there.
`width` on a column sets its heading's width, `nowrap` keeps a value on one
line and `align: 'end'` right-aligns numbers.

### Corners

The box's corners follow where it sits: `radius.lg` on the page, `md` in a
Card, `sm` deeper, and a control in a cell sits one level deeper still. See
[corners](../corners.md).

## Do / don't

- Do use one table per dataset, with the same fields in every row.
- Do right-align numeric columns with `align: 'end'`.
- Don't use a table for layout; use `Space`.

modules.title: Alert
modules.description: A tinted box for a status message in the page flow, with an optional title, icon and action.
modules.importLine: import { Alert, type AlertProps, type AlertTone } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A tinted, bordered box for a status message that sits in the page flow: a tone,
an optional title, body text, an optional icon and an optional action. The
tone's `theme.color.chip[tone]` colours the background, border, title and icon;
the body text uses the normal text colour so a sentence stays readable.

Use something else for: inline field or form failure text (`ErrorMessage`), or a
single status word in a row (`Chip`). An Alert is for a message with weight that
may carry an action.

## Usage

### Choosing a tone

- `warning`: needs attention (overdue, about to expire).
- `danger`: something failed.
- `success`: something finished.
- `info`: neutral news.

`warning` and `danger` render `role="alert"` and are announced the moment they
mount; `success` and `info` render `role="status"` and are announced politely.

### Behaviour

- Corners follow surface depth (see [corners](../corners.md)): 16px on a Page,
  8px in a Card. With no provider the Alert counts as depth 0.
- Its contents, including `action`, sit one level deeper, so a Button in the
  action is already one step smaller than the Alert. Do not pass `radius`.
- There is no default icon per tone; pass `Icon` when you want one.
- Spacing and font sizes come from theme tokens; there is no `style` prop.

## Do / don't

- Do pick the tone by meaning, not by colour.
- Do put the one recovery action in `action`.
- Don't use it for field errors; use `ErrorMessage`.
- Don't mount a `danger` or `warning` Alert for static, always-visible copy:
  it is announced as an alert when it appears.

modules.body:
The centred "nothing here" block a screen shows in place of a list: a title
line and an optional faint second line, with generous vertical padding
(`4rem`). Also used for a list's loading and error states.

Use something else for: an empty message *inside* a `Card` (a plain
left-aligned line of card content reads right there), transient feedback
(`useToast`).

## Usage

### Choosing a title and second line

Keep `title` short and say what is not here. Put the explanation or next step
in `children`. Only `undefined` omits the second line; `null` renders an empty
one.

### Styling

No `className`. It renders plain `div`s with no `role`; it is not a live
region.

## Do / don't

- Do use it directly on the page background, as a sibling of the Cards.
- Do keep `title` short; put the explanation or next step in `children`.
- Don't set `danger` for "no results"; that is not an error.
- Don't pass `null` as `children` expecting no second line: only `undefined`
  omits it (`null` renders an empty second line).

modules.title: ErrorMessage
modules.description: A failure message the user must notice, announced to screen readers and rendered nothing when empty.
modules.importLine: import { ErrorMessage, type ErrorMessageProps } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A failure message the user must notice. It renders a `

` in the danger colour at `fontSize.sm`, with no margin or padding, so screen readers announce it when it appears. Use something else for: static red copy that is always on screen (``, which uses the darker chip red and no `role`), or a boxed message with a tone and an action (`Alert`). ## Usage ### Behaviour - Empty renders nothing, not an empty alert. Leave it mounted and pass the error (or `undefined`) as children; an alert region that appears with text is announced. - `0` is not empty and renders. - Space it from the field above with `Space` `gap`; it has no margin. - Every other HTML attribute (`id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event handlers) passes through, and may override `role`. ### Linking it to a field Give the message an `id` and set `aria-describedby` on a native control to that `id`, so assistive tech reads the error with the field: ```tsx {error} ``` `TextInput` takes no `id` or `aria-*` props, so it cannot be linked this way; place the message below it. ### Styling There is no `style` prop. Override with `className` at `'&&'` specificity, never `!important`. ## Do / don't - Do keep it mounted and pass `error` as children. - Do link it to a native field with `id` and `aria-describedby`. - Don't use it for permanent red copy; use ``. - Don't add margins to it; use `Space`.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description:
Keep it mounted and pass the error as `children`: it is announced when text
appears and renders nothing when `children` is `undefined`.

examples.title: Under a field
examples.description:
Space it from the field above with `Space` `gap`; it has no margin. The
message shows while the title is empty and goes away once one is typed.

examples.title: The rendered element
examples.description: `as` picks the element: `p`, `div` or `span`. Each one keeps `role="alert"`.

examples.title: What counts as empty
examples.description:
`undefined`, `null`, `false` and `''` render nothing, not an empty alert.
`0` is not empty and renders.

import { ErrorMessage, Space, Text } from '@korzun/design/component';

export default function EmptyChildren() {
  return (
    <Space direction="vertical" gap="sm">
      <Space>
        <Text tone="muted" size="sm">
          undefined:
        </Text>
        <ErrorMessage>{undefined}</ErrorMessage>
      </Space>
      <Space>
        <Text tone="muted" size="sm">
          null:
        </Text>
        <ErrorMessage>{null}</ErrorMessage>
      </Space>
      <Space>
        <Text tone="muted" size="sm">
          false:
        </Text>
        <ErrorMessage>{false}</ErrorMessage>
      </Space>
      <Space>
        <Text tone="muted" size="sm">
          empty string:
        </Text>
        <ErrorMessage>{''}</ErrorMessage>
      </Space>
      <Space>
        <Text tone="muted" size="sm">
          0:
        </Text>
        <ErrorMessage>{0}</ErrorMessage>
      </Space>
    </Space>
  );
}

modules.title: ProgressCircle
modules.description: A progress circle, filled like a pie or border-only, in a tone, with its value beside it, inside it or hidden.
modules.importLine: import { ProgressCircle, type ProgressCircleProps, type ProgressCircleTone } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A circle that fills as `value` goes from 0 to `max`: a pie inside a thin ring
(`variant="filled"`) or an arc over a faint track (`variant="outline"`), in a
`tone`. The value is written beside it, inside it, or not at all (`label`), as
a percentage or with your own `unit`. The whole thing is one
`role="progressbar"` named by `ariaLabel`, whose `aria-valuetext` is the same
text the label shows.

It shows a number at every value, 0 and `max` included. For words at the ends
("Not started", "Completed"), use the [Reading progress](../recipes/reading-progress.md)
recipe.

Use something else for: an indeterminate wait (`Spinner`, or `loading` on
a `Button`), a pull-to-refresh indicator (`usePullToRefresh`).

## Usage

### Surprising behaviour

- `max` defaults to 1, so `value` is a fraction: passing `42` clamps to 1 and
  shows "100%". Pass `max={100}` for a 0–100 value.
- The percentage is `Math.round`ed, so `0.996` shows "100%" next to a
  near-full circle. Other units show the value to one decimal at most.
- `unit` is appended verbatim: write `" pages"`, with the space, for "3 pages".
- A value that is not a finite number (`NaN`, or `undefined` from a cleared
  field) counts as 0.
- An inside label longer than four characters is squeezed to fit, so keep it
  short (a percentage, or a bare number with `unit=""`), and use `size` 40 or
  more.

### Styling

No `className`. Colour comes from `tone`; a filled circle's ring is
`text.primary` and an outline's track is `border.default`.

## Do / don't

- Do write an `ariaLabel` that names the thing in progress.
- Do pick `outline` with `label="inside"`; text over a filled pie needs its halo.
- Don't render your own "42%" next to it; set `label` instead.
- Don't use it for indeterminate loading.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: By default `value` is a fraction from 0 to 1, not a percentage: `0.42` shows "42%". The circle shows at 0 and 1 too, as "0%" and "100%". `ariaLabel` names the progress for assistive tech. The buttons step the value by a tenth.

examples.title: Filled and outline
examples.description: `variant="filled"` is a pie inside a ring; `variant="outline"` is border-only, an arc over a faint track. `label` puts the value `'outside'` (the default), `'inside'` the circle, or nowhere (`'none'`, still read by screen readers).

examples.title: Tones
examples.description: `tone` colours the progress: `brand` (the default), a status colour, or a quiet `neutral` grey. The ring of a filled circle stays in the text colour.

examples.title: Max and units
examples.description: `max` is the value that means done (default 1, a fraction). The default `unit`, `'%'`, shows the percentage of `max`; any other `unit` shows the value itself followed by it, verbatim, so include a leading space when you want one.
examples.code:
import { ProgressCircle, Space, Text } from '@korzun/design/component';

export default function Units() {
  return (
    <Space direction="vertical" gap="sm">
      <Space>
        <ProgressCircle value={42} max={100} ariaLabel="Upload progress" />
        <Text tone="muted">value 42, max 100</Text>
      </Space>
      <Space>
        <ProgressCircle value={3} max={12} unit=" of 12" ariaLabel="Chapters read" />
        <Text tone="muted">value 3, max 12, unit " of 12"</Text>
      </Space>
      <Space>
        <ProgressCircle value={180} max={320} unit=" pages" ariaLabel="Pages read" />
        <Text tone="muted">value 180, max 320, unit " pages"</Text>
      </Space>
      <Space>
        <ProgressCircle
          value={7}
          max={10}
          unit=""
          label="inside"
          variant="outline"
          size={48}
          ariaLabel="Steps done"
        />
        <Text tone="muted">value 7, max 10, unit "", inside</Text>
      </Space>
    </Space>
  );
}

rows.description: Accessible name of the progressbar: say what progress it is (`Reading progress for ${title}`), because a bare "42%" means nothing out of context.

rows.name: label
rows.description: Where the value is written: `'outside'` beside the circle, `'inside'` centred in it (suits `variant="outline"`, and sizes of 40 or more), or `'none'` (screen readers still hear it). The text is never "Not started" or "Completed"; see the Reading progress recipe for those.

rows.name: max
rows.description: The value that means done. The default, 1, takes a fraction (`0.42`); pass `100` for a percentage or `12` for 12 chapters.

rows.name: size
rows.description: Width and height of the circle in px. An outside label keeps its `fontSize.sm`; an inside one scales with the circle.

rows.name: tone
rows.description: Colour of the progress: `'brand'` (default), a status colour (`'success'`, `'warning'`, `'danger'`, `'info'`) or `'neutral'` grey.

rows.name: unit
rows.description: How the value is written. `'%'` (the default) shows the percentage of `max`, rounded to a whole number. Anything else shows the value itself followed by `unit`, verbatim: `unit=" of 12"` shows "3 of 12", `unit=""` the bare number. Screen readers hear the same text.

rows.name: value
rows.description: Progress from 0 to `max`. Clamped to that range; a value that is not a finite number (`NaN`, `undefined`, `Infinity`) counts as 0.

rows.name: variant
rows.description: `'filled'` is a pie: a sector inside a thin ring. `'outline'` is border-only: an arc over a faint track, with the middle empty.

tables.name: ProgressCircleTone

changelog.text: **Breaking:** `ProgressIndicator` is renamed `ProgressCircle` (`ProgressIndicatorProps` → `ProgressCircleProps`). It always draws the circle and writes a number, 0 and 1 included; "Not started" and "Completed" are gone from the component and live in the new Reading progress recipe. The whole mark, label included, is now one `progressbar` with `aria-valuetext`.

New props: `tone` (`brand`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `neutral`; new `ProgressCircleTone` type), `variant="outline"` for a border-only arc instead of the filled pie, `label` (`outside`, `inside`, `none`) for where the value is written, and `max` and `unit` for values that are not fractions (`value={3} max={12} unit=" of 12"` shows "3 of 12").
A `value` that is not a finite number (`NaN`, `undefined`, `Infinity`) shows "Not started" instead of "NaN%".

modules.title: Spinner
modules.description: A rotating loading indicator that takes the surrounding text colour and size.
modules.importLine: import { Spinner, type SpinnerProps } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A rotating loading indicator. It is `1em` square, takes the surrounding text
colour (`currentColor`), and by default the surrounding font size, so it sits
inline with text without any sizing. Use it for a page, panel or inline load
that has no progress value.

Use something else for: a load with a known fraction (`ProgressCircle`).
`Button` (`loading`), `Select` (`loading`) and `Switch` (`loading`) draw their
own spinner; do not add one beside them.

## Usage

### Behaviour

- By default the root is a `span` with `role="status"` and `aria-label={label}`,
  so a screen reader announces the load. The inner icon is always `aria-hidden`.
- With `decorative`, the root has no role and is `aria-hidden`.
- Override with `className` at `'&&'` specificity, never `!important`.

### Styling

There is no `style` prop and no other attribute passthrough.

## Do / don't

- Do use `decorative` when adjacent text names the load.
- Do give a specific `label` when the spinner stands alone.
- Don't hand-write `role="status"` around it; it already has one.
- Don't add a Spinner inside `Button`, `Select` or `Switch`; they draw their
  own.

examples.title: Basic

        <Text tone="muted">xxs</Text>
      </Space>
      <Space>
        <Spinner size="xs" label="Loading, xs" />
        <Text tone="muted">xs</Text>
      </Space>
      <Space>
        <Spinner size="sm" label="Loading, sm" />

      </Space>
      <Space>
        <Spinner size="xxl" label="Loading, xxl" />
        <Text tone="muted">xxl</Text>
      </Space>
    </Space>
  );
}

modules.title: Toast
modules.description: Short, transient confirmations and errors that slide in from a corner and leave on their own.
modules.importLine: import { ToastProvider, useToast, type ToastProviderProps } from '@korzun/design/toast'
modules.body:
Short, transient confirmations and errors ("Password changed", "Failed to reset
password") that appear in a corner, stay four seconds, and slide away. Mount
`ToastProvider` once; call the function `useToast()` returns from anywhere
below it.

Use something else for: an error that must stay until the user acts (inline
text near the field, or `EmptyState danger` for a failed load), a question
needing an answer (`ConfirmModal`).

## Usage

### `ToastProvider`

Placement:

- **Inside `ThemeProvider`** (toasts are styled from the theme) and above every
  component that calls `useToast`. Bookplate nests it innermost among its app
  providers, around the router.
- It renders its container itself; you don't place anything in the layout.
  Desktop: bottom-right, `space.xxxxl` from the edges. Mobile: full width just
  above the floating `NavMobile` (and below it in z-order, so toasts slide up
  from behind the bar).
- The container is a `popover="manual"` element shown while any toast is up,
  so toasts appear **above an open modal `<dialog>`** too.

```tsx
<ThemeProvider identity={username}>
  <ToastProvider>
    <AppRouter />
  </ToastProvider>
</ThemeProvider>
```

### `useToast()`

```ts
useToast(): (message: string, type: 'success' | 'error' | 'info') => void
```

Returns the **function itself** (not an object): `const showToast = useToast()`.

| Argument | Notes |
|---|---|
| `message` | Plain string. No elements, no actions, no links. |
| `type` | `'success'`: green check. `'error'`: red X, announced `aria-live="assertive"`. `'info'`: brand-blue info icon. Success and info are `polite`. Required; there is no default. |

### Behaviour to know

- **Without a `ToastProvider` above it, `showToast` silently does nothing**
  (the default context is a no-op). No error is thrown.
- Duration is fixed at 4000ms; there is no per-toast duration, no close
  button, and no tap-to-dismiss.
- Toasts have `radius.md` (a floating layer) per [corners](corners.md).

### Styling

No `className`. Position, colours and corners come from theme tokens.

## Do / don't

- Do mount exactly one `ToastProvider`, inside `ThemeProvider`.
- Do keep messages to one short sentence; nothing truncates a long one.
- Don't destructure: `const { showToast } = useToast()` is wrong.
- Don't use a toast for the only copy of an error the user must fix.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: `useToast` returns a function that takes a one-line message and a `type`. `success` shows a green check, `error` a red X and is announced assertively, and `info` a blue info icon.

examples.title: Reporting an outcome
examples.description: A form submitted from the Card footer reports its result with the function `useToast` returns. A failed save also puts the message in an `ErrorMessage` beside the field, so the toast is never the only copy of an error the user must fix.

examples.title: Limiting the stack
examples.description: `maxToasts` caps how many toasts show at once: when a new one would exceed it, the oldest starts to leave. It goes on the app's one root `ToastProvider`; here the cap is two, so the third click pushes the first toast out.

modules.title: Icons
modules.description: Inline SVG icon components that take the surrounding text colour, with the shared IconProps.
modules.importLine: import { AdjustmentsHorizontalIcon, AlertOctagonIcon, BookIcon, BooksIcon, CheckIcon, ChevronCircleIcon, ChevronIcon, CircleXIcon, ClockIcon, DeviceIcon, HandLoveYouIcon, HandOkIcon, HandPeaceIcon, HandsClapIcon, HomeIcon, InfoCircleIcon, KeyIcon, ListCheckIcon, MoreIcon, RowRemoveIcon, SearchIcon, SettingsIcon, SpinnerIcon, ThumbDownIcon, UploadIcon, UserIcon, UsersIcon, XIcon, defaultFilledIconProps, defaultStrokeIconProps, type IconProps } from '@korzun/design/icon'
modules.body:
Inline SVG icon components, mostly from [Tabler](https://tabler.io/icons) on a
24×24 view box. Each one paints in `currentColor`, so it takes the text colour
of wherever it sits, in both themes, including hover and selected states.

Use something else for: a determinate progress mark (`ProgressCircle`), a
loading state on a button (`Button`'s `loading`, which draws the spinner for
you).

## Usage

### Props

Every icon takes the same `IconProps`, listed below. `defaultStrokeIconProps`
and `defaultFilledIconProps` are exported for building your own icon with the
same defaults.

### Sizing and colour

- Size with `width`/`height` props (`<HomeIcon width={14} height={14} />`), or
  with `height: '1em', width: '1em'` in a class so it scales with the text (this
  is what `Button` does for `prefix`/`suffix`).
- Colour by setting `color` on the icon or any ancestor. Don't pass `stroke` or
  `fill` colours; they bypass the theme.

### Passing icons to other components

Components take the icon **component**, never an element:

```tsx
<Button prefix={SearchIcon}>Search</Button>                 // ComponentType<IconProps>
<ConfirmModal icon={AlertOctagonIcon} danger … />
const item: NavItem = { to: '/', label: 'Home', Icon: HomeIcon, active };
options={[{ value: 'grid', label: 'Grid', Icon: BooksIcon }]} // SegmentedControl
```

### Kinds of icon

Every icon is listed in the table below, and the docs site also shows them as a grid. Each is one of three kinds.

- **Stroke** icons draw outlines and take `stroke` and `strokeWidth`.
- **Filled** icons (`AlertOctagonIcon`, `CheckIcon`, `CircleXIcon`,
  `InfoCircleIcon`) ignore `stroke` and `strokeWidth`.
- **Emoji** icons (`HandLoveYouIcon`, `HandOkIcon`, `HandPeaceIcon`,
  `HandsClapIcon`, `ThumbDownIcon`) draw the platform's colour-emoji glyph as an
  alpha mask over `currentColor`, so they recolour like the others but their
  exact shape depends on the OS emoji font. They ignore `fill`, `stroke` and
  `strokeWidth`.

Two to know: `ChevronIcon` points right, so rotate it via `className` for other
directions. `SpinnerIcon` is a quarter arc that **does not spin by itself**; use
`Spinner` (component) for a ready-made loader, not a hand-built `SpinnerIcon`:

```tsx
<Spinner label="Loading books" />
```

### Every icon

| Export | Kind | Depicts |
|---|---|---|
| `AdjustmentsHorizontalIcon` | stroke | Three horizontal sliders (general settings, filters). |
| `AlertOctagonIcon` | filled | Octagon with `!` (danger/warning; confirm modals). |
| `BookIcon` | stroke | A single book (Tabler `book-2`). |
| `BooksIcon` | stroke | Books standing on a shelf. |
| `CheckIcon` | filled | A check mark (success). |
| `ChevronCircleIcon` | stroke | Right chevron in a circle (Card's collapse toggle). |
| `ChevronIcon` | stroke | Right-pointing chevron; rotate it via `className` for other directions. |
| `CircleXIcon` | filled | X in a filled circle (clear, error). |
| `ClockIcon` | stroke | Clock face (time, pending). |
| `DeviceIcon` | stroke | A tablet / e-reader (Tabler `device-tablet`). |
| `HandLoveYouIcon` | emoji | 🤟 silhouette (rating 5, "Love"). |
| `HandOkIcon` | emoji | 👌 silhouette (rating 2, "Okay"). |
| `HandPeaceIcon` | emoji | ✌️ silhouette (rating 3, "Nice"). |
| `HandsClapIcon` | emoji | 👏 silhouette (rating 4, "Great"). |
| `HomeIcon` | stroke | A house. |
| `InfoCircleIcon` | filled | `i` in a filled circle (info). |
| `KeyIcon` | stroke | A key (passwords, credentials). |
| `ListCheckIcon` | stroke | Checklist (requests, tasks). |
| `MoreIcon` | stroke | Three horizontal dots (overflow menu). |
| `RowRemoveIcon` | stroke | A table row with an X under it (remove row). |
| `SearchIcon` | stroke | Magnifying glass. |
| `SettingsIcon` | stroke | Gear. |
| `SpinnerIcon` | stroke | A quarter arc. **Does not spin by itself**; use `Spinner` (component) for a ready-made loader. |
| `ThumbDownIcon` | emoji | 👎 silhouette (rating 1, "Bad"). |
| `UploadIcon` | stroke | Arrow up out of a tray. |
| `UserIcon` | stroke | One person. |
| `UsersIcon` | stroke | Two people. |
| `XIcon` | stroke | An X (close, dismiss, error toast). |

## Do / don't

- Do pass `aria-hidden` when the icon sits next to a text label.
- Do give a standalone meaningful icon `role` and `aria-label`.
- Don't pass `<Icon />` elements where a component is expected.
- Don't import from icon file paths; only `@korzun/design/icon` is exported.

modules.title: Theme
modules.description: ThemeProvider, the light and dark themes, and createUseStyles for writing token-based styles.
modules.importLine: import { GlobalStyles, ThemeProvider, createUseStyles, darkTheme, lightTheme, useTheme, useThemeGlobalStyles, useThemeSetting, type SpaceValue, type Theme, type ThemeMode, type ThemeProviderProps, type ThemeSetting } from '@korzun/design/theme'
modules.body:
Every visual value comes from the theme. App styles use `createUseStyles` (the
same function react-jss exports, re-exported here) with a typed `theme`
argument. Don't add another CSS-in-JS library, and don't write literal colours,
spacing, font sizes, or radii.

Use something else for: a ready-made light/dark/auto picker (`ThemeSetting`),
the full list of token keys ([tokens](tokens.md)).

## Usage

### Setup

```tsx
<ThemeProvider identity={userId /* or null when signed out */}>
  <ToastProvider>{app}</ToastProvider>
</ThemeProvider>
```

- `ThemeProvider` renders `GlobalStyles`: the page background, the body font,
  a 16px input floor on iOS, scroll lock while a `<dialog>` is open, and the
  `theme-rotation` and `theme-slide-*` keyframes. Don't render
  `GlobalStyles` yourself, or `useThemeGlobalStyles()`, the hook it calls.
- `lightTheme` / `darkTheme` are the two concrete themes (for tests).

### `useThemeSetting()`

```ts
useThemeSetting(): [ThemeSetting, (setting: ThemeSetting) => void]
```

Returns `[setting, setSetting]`, where `ThemeSetting` is `'light' | 'dark' |
'auto'`. `'auto'` follows the OS `prefers-color-scheme` live. The
`ThemeSetting` component is a ready-made picker for it. Without a
`ThemeProvider` above it, the setter does nothing.

### `useTheme()`

```ts
useTheme(): Theme
```

Returns the current `Theme` object, for values needed outside a stylesheet.
`theme.colorScheme` is the mode it resolved to, `'light'` or `'dark'`.

### Writing styles

```ts
// style.ts, next to the component
import { createUseStyles, type Theme } from '@korzun/design/theme';
import { applyTransparency } from '@korzun/design';

export const useStyle = createUseStyles((theme: Theme) => ({
  root: {
    padding: theme.space.md,
    backgroundColor: theme.color.bg.card,
  },
  highlight: { backgroundColor: applyTransparency(theme.color.brand.default, 0.12) },
  [theme.breakpoint.mobile]: { root: { padding: theme.space.sm } },
}));
```

- Style files are for padding, borders, backgrounds, and one-offs (borders come from the border tokens). Lay out with
  `Space` and set text with `Text`/`Heading`.
- `applyTransparency(color, alpha)` turns a hex or rgb token into an `rgba()`
  string. Use it for tints instead of writing an rgba literal.
- Media queries: use the `theme.breakpoint.mobile` / `.normal` strings as keys.

### Tokens

The token groups (`color`, `space`, `radius`, `fontSize`, `shadow`, `zIndex`,
`breakpoint` and the rest) are listed key by key in [tokens](tokens.md). Use the
semantic tokens, never the primitive `gray`, `blue` and `red` scales. Radii are
chosen by nesting depth; see [corners](corners.md).

| Group | Keys | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `color.text` | `primary`, `secondary`, `muted`, `faint`, `description`, `onPrimary`, `onDanger` | `muted` for labels and meta, `faint` for placeholders |
| `color.bg` | `page`, `card`, `cardHeader`, `track`, `switchOff`, `input`, `footer`, `glass`, `glassFallback`, `glassActive`, `selected`, `hover`, `success`, `placeholder` | `cardHeader` is also the shaded-row and inset-box fill; `hover` is a translucent scrim |
| `color.border` | `default`, `strong`, `light`, `focus`, `hover`, `danger`, `glass`, `glassActive`, `faint`, `loading`, `success`, `section` | Cards and dividers use `strong`; inputs use `default`; `light` is a hairline rule inside a card |
| `color.brand` | `default`, `hover`, `active`, `light`, `outline`, `loading*`, `linkHover` | The primary action colour |
| `color.danger` | `default`, `hover`, `active`, `light`, `outline`, `loading*` | Destructive actions and errors |
| `color.success` | (a string) | Solid green |
| `color.warning` | (a string) | Solid amber |
| `color.info` | (a string) | Solid blue, the mode's `brand.default` |
| `color.chip.<tone>` | `{ text, bg, border }` for 13 tones. Status tones: `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `neutral`. Label tones: `status`, `author`, `series`, `subject`, `book`, `entryType`, `user`, `rating` | Used by `Chip`; `neutral` text holds 4.5:1 on its tint |
| `color.overlay` | `backdrop` | Modal backdrop |
| `color.gray` / `blue` / `red` | primitive scales | Don't use these in app code; use the semantic tokens above |
| `space` | `xxxs` 0.1rem, `xxs` 0.125, `xs` 0.25, `sm` 0.375, `md` 0.5, `lg` 0.625, `xl` 0.75, `xxl` 1, `xxxl` 1.25, `xxxxl` 1.5, `xxxxxl` 2rem | `md` is the default gap between stacked fields |
| `radius` | `sm` 4px, `md` 8px, `lg` 16px, `circle`, `pill` | Chosen by nesting depth; see [corners](corners.md) |
| `fontSize` | `xxs` 0.6rem, `xs` 0.7, `sm` 0.75, `md` 0.875, `lg` 1, `xl` 1.25, `xxl` 1.75rem | Control text is `'0.80rem'`, the one sanctioned literal (already applied by `recipe.input` and Button) |
| `fontWeight` | `regular` 400, `medium` 500, `semibold` 600, `bold` 700, `extrabold` 800 | |
| `lineHeight` | `tight` 1, `body` 1.3 | |
| `fontFamily` | `body`, `mono` | |
| `shadow` | `card`, `cardStack`, `hoverLift`, `dangerStack`, `brandStack`, `glass`, `glassActive` | Floating layers use `hoverLift` |
| `transition` | `fast`, `medium`, `slide`, `slow`, `spring` | Values like `'0.2s ease-in'` |
| `zIndex` | `behind`, `base`, `stack.{lo,md,hi}`, `header`, `sticky`, `toast` | |
| `breakpoint` | `mobile` (≤640px), `normal` | Media query strings |
| `layout` | `navHeightMobile`, `modalWidth`, `controlHeight`, `floatingControlTopBase` | Measured chrome sizes to lay out around |

### Recipes

Recipes are style fragments that you spread into a rule: `{ ...theme.recipe.input }`.

| Recipe | Gives you |
|---|---|
| `recipe.input` | Text-input chrome: font, `md` radius, border, hover and focus colours, iOS 16px floor; `&$danger` turns the border red if your sheet declares a `danger: {}` class |
| `recipe.label` | Field label: semibold, `md`, muted; `&$danger` |
| `recipe.focusRing` | Transparent 2px outline; set `outlineColor: theme.color.brand.outline` on `'&:focus'` |
| `recipe.spinner` | 1em rotating box. `Spinner` is the normal way to show a spinner; use the recipe only for a custom rotating element |
| `recipe.glass` / `glassHighlight` | Frosted translucent surface (floating chrome) and its active state |
| `recipe.row` | The shaded field row a control sits in inside a card: `bg.cardHeader`, `md` corners, padding `md lg md sm`. Use it for custom rows next to form fields |
| `recipe.card.shell` / `header` / `footer` | The Card surface (`lg`), its header bar, and its footer bar |
| `recipe.modal.dialog` / `header` / `footer` | A `<dialog>` surface (`lg`, shared width, backdrop), its title, and its button bar |

Recipes that use `$name` references need an empty class with that name in the
same sheet (`danger: {}`).

## Do / don't

- Do style with `theme.*` tokens and `createUseStyles`.
- Do use `applyTransparency` for a tint instead of an rgba literal.
- Don't render `GlobalStyles` yourself; `ThemeProvider` does.
- Don't use the primitive `gray`, `blue` and `red` scales in app code.

changelog.text: **Breaking:** `size.metadataValue` (and the `size` group) is removed; `MetadataList` was its only user.

New `color.code` palette (foreground, keyword, string, function, parameter, constant, punctuation, comment, link) for syntax colours, and `recipe.codeBlock`, `recipe.inlineCode` and `recipe.codeColours` (the ten `--code-*` variables Shiki's css-variables theme reads, from `color.code`) for code rendered outside `CodeBlock` and `Code`.

`GlobalStyles` (rendered by `ThemeProvider`) ships the reset the components are drawn against: every element is `box-sizing: border-box` with no default margin or padding, as in Bookplate's and Scribe's `index.html`. Without it a text field was 51px tall instead of `layout.controlHeight` (33px). An app that already carries this reset sees no change; one that relied on browser default margins (`p`, `h1`, `ul`) loses them.

`color-scheme` is set on `html` as well as `body`. With body alone the root's scheme was `normal`, so in dark mode the page scrollbar stayed light and an iframe whose document uses `GlobalStyles` (or is still loading) painted an opaque white box.

The unchecked track is the new `color.bg.switchOff` token (`#868686` light, `#6E7480` dark), about 3:1 on `bg.page`, `bg.card` and `bg.cardHeader`; it was `border.default` (1.16:1 on a shaded row). The loading spinner on an unchecked track is now the thumb colour.

Dark `color.border.light` is `#333439` (was `#2B2C30`, 1.10:1 on `bg.page` and 1.23:1 on `bg.card`, so hairline rules all but vanished); it is now 1.24:1 and 1.39:1, at or above light mode's step. A loading `Select`'s border in dark is a shade lighter. Light is unchanged.

`color.chip.neutral` text is a step stronger, so a neutral Tag or chip holds 4.5:1 on its tint over `bg.page`, `bg.card` and `bg.cardHeader`: light `#5E5E5E` (was `#6E6E6E`, 4.0:1 over `cardHeader`), dark `#A8ADB6`, the mode's `text.description` (was `#9CA1AB`, 4.47:1 over `page`). Fill and border are unchanged.
New `theme.layout.formWidth` (`400px`): the width of a standalone form column such as sign-in, narrower than a dialog.
New `fontWeight.regular` (400) token.

`Tag` status tones: `success`, `warning` (yellow, stronger fill), `danger`, `info` (brand blue). New `color.warning` and `color.info` solid colours. Status tones report state; label tones name things. No visual change to existing tags.
New `theme.recipe.row`: the shaded field row (`bg.cardHeader`, `radius.md`, padding `md lg md sm`), for custom rows beside form fields. `Switch`'s horizontal layout now uses it and looks the same.
New `color.chip.neutral` token: a quiet grey built from each mode's muted text colour (light 0.08 / 0.22 alphas, dark 0.16 / 0.30, matching the other chips in each mode).
Theme tokens and light/dark themes; `ThemeProvider` takes an `identity` prop (replaces Bookplate's token coupling).

modules.title: ThemeSetting
modules.description: A ready-made "Appearance" card with a Light, Dark and Auto switch bound to the theme.
modules.importLine: import { ThemeSetting, type ThemeSettingProps } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A ready-made settings feature: a `Card` titled "Appearance" holding a
three-option `SegmentedControl` (Light / Dark / Auto) bound to the theme. A
choice applies immediately and is persisted by `ThemeProvider`.

Use something else for: reading the current choice or the resolved mode in
your own code (`useThemeSetting` from `@korzun/design/theme`), a custom
appearance UI (build it on `useThemeSetting`).

## Usage

### Props and styling

It takes no props: no `className`, no title override.

### How it works

- Reads and writes through `useThemeSetting()`, i.e. the context provided by
  `ThemeProvider` from `@korzun/design/theme`.
- `ThemeProvider` stores the choice in `localStorage` under
  `theme-setting:<identity>`, where `identity` is the provider's prop (for
  example the signed-in username). Switching identity restores that user's
  choice; without an `identity` (or with `identity={null}`) it **stores
  nothing** and the setting resets to `'auto'` on reload.
- `'auto'` follows the OS `prefers-color-scheme` live.

### Behaviour to know

- **Without a `ThemeProvider` above it, it renders but does nothing**: the
  default context's setter is a no-op.
- **Name clash at the package root:** `@korzun/design` (root entry) exports
  this component as `ThemeSetting` and the `'light' | 'dark' | 'auto'` type as
  `ThemeSettingValue`. From `@korzun/design/theme` the type is named
  `ThemeSetting`. Import the component from `/component` to avoid confusion.

### In an app

Give the provider an identity so the choice persists per user, and place the
setting in a `Page` like any other Card:

```tsx
<ThemeProvider identity={viewer?.username ?? null}>
  <ToastProvider>
    <AppRouter />
  </ToastProvider>
</ThemeProvider>

<Page bottomNav>
  <ThemeSetting />
  <Card title="Change password">…</Card>
</Page>
```

## Do / don't

- Do place it directly in a `Page`, like any other Card.
- Do pass `identity` to `ThemeProvider` if the choice should survive a reload.
- Don't wrap it in another `Card`; it already is one.

modules.title: useIsStandalone
modules.description: True when running as the installed app (added to the home screen); gates install-only chrome.
modules.importLine: import { useIsStandalone } from '@korzun/design/hooks'
modules.body:
True when running as the installed app (added to the home screen). Part of the
mobile-chrome behaviour shared by the layout components, with
[`useMinimizeOnScroll`](use-minimize-on-scroll.md) and
[`usePullToRefresh`](use-pull-to-refresh.md).

## Usage

### `useIsStandalone()`

```ts
useIsStandalone(): boolean
```

True when running as an installed PWA (added to the home screen):
`(display-mode: standalone)` matches, or iOS Safari's
`navigator.standalone === true`. A hook: call it at the top of a component,
not inside a condition, loop or event handler, and pass the result down. It
subscribes to the display-mode query, so the component re-renders if the mode
changes. During server rendering it returns `false` without touching `window`;
on the client it corrects itself after hydration.

```tsx
const standalone = useIsStandalone();
return standalone ? <TopFade /> : null;
```

Use it to gate chrome that only makes sense when installed: `TopFade` and a
pull-to-refresh indicator ([`usePullToRefresh`](use-pull-to-refresh.md#a-pull-to-refresh-indicator)).

## Do / don't

- Do gate pull-to-refresh UI on `useIsStandalone()`; browser tabs have their own.
- Don't call it inside `&&` or an `if`: read it once at the top, then branch on the value.

examples.description:
True only in the installed app (added to the home screen). Here, in a browser tab, it is

changelog.text: **Breaking:** `isStandalone()` is now the hook `useIsStandalone()`, built on `useSyncExternalStore`. Call it at the top of a component and branch on its value (`const standalone = useIsStandalone();` then `{standalone && <TopFade />}`), not inside a condition or callback. It re-renders when the display mode changes and returns `false` during server rendering instead of throwing on `window`.
Hooks: `useMinimizeOnScroll`, `usePullToRefresh`, `isStandalone`.

modules.title: useMinimizeOnScroll
modules.description: Minimizes bottom chrome on a fast scroll down and expands it on the way back up, like the iOS tab bar.
modules.importLine: import { EXPAND_AFTER, MINIMIZE_SPEED, useMinimizeOnScroll, type MinimizeOnScroll } from '@korzun/design/hooks'
modules.body:
Minimizes bottom chrome on a fast scroll down and expands it on the way back
up, like the iOS tab bar. Part of the mobile-chrome behaviour shared by the
layout components, with [`useIsStandalone`](use-is-standalone.md) and
[`usePullToRefresh`](use-pull-to-refresh.md). It reads the **window**
scroller; it does nothing for content scrolling in an inner `overflow: auto`
element.

## Usage

### `useMinimizeOnScroll({ resetKey })`

```ts
useMinimizeOnScroll({ resetKey }: { resetKey: string }): MinimizeOnScroll
type MinimizeOnScroll = { minimized: boolean; expand: () => void }
```

iOS-tab-bar behaviour for bottom chrome. `NavMobile` already uses it; call it
yourself only for other chrome.

- Minimizes when one scroll frame moves **down** at `>= MINIMIZE_SPEED`
  (`0.8` px/ms). Speed, not distance: slow reading never minimizes.
- Expands after scrolling **up** `EXPAND_AFTER` (`12`) px back from the furthest-down point
  reached since minimizing, on reaching the top, or when you call `expand()`.
- Only user-driven scrolls count: it ignores scrolling until a `touchstart` or
  `wheel` is seen after `resetKey` last changed (so scroll restoration doesn't
  minimize it). Changing `resetKey` also expands. Pass the route's
  `useLocation().key`.
- iOS rubber-band overscroll (top and bottom) is clamped out.

## Do / don't

- Don't call `useMinimizeOnScroll` for the bar `NavMobile` already manages.
- Don't expect it to track a nested scroll container.

modules.title: useModal
modules.description: A hook that drives a native dialog element from an open flag and routes Escape and backdrop clicks to a dismiss callback.
modules.importLine: import { useModal } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A hook that drives a native `<dialog>` from an `isOpen` boolean: it calls
`showModal()` / `close()` for you and routes Escape and backdrop clicks to
`onDismiss`. It is the base under [`Modal`](modal.md) (and so `ConfirmModal`).
Reach for `Modal` first; this hook remains for modals `Modal` cannot express,
built from this hook plus the `theme.recipe.modal.*` styles.

Use something else for: a plain yes/no confirmation (`ConfirmModal`), or a
dropdown or non-modal floating layer (`Popover`).

## Usage

### Signature

```ts
function useModal(
  isOpen: boolean,
  onDismiss: () => void,
  canDismiss?: boolean, // default true
): RefObject<HTMLDialogElement | null>;
```

| Argument | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isOpen` | `boolean` | (required) | The single source of truth. `true` calls `showModal()`, `false` calls `close()`. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | (required) | Called on Escape and on a backdrop click. **It does not close anything itself**: set your `isOpen` state to `false` in it. Receives no event. |
| `canDismiss` | `boolean` | `true` | When `false`, Escape and backdrop clicks are swallowed. Pass `!loading` (or `countdown === 0`) so an in-flight request can't be escaped. |

Returns a ref to attach to the `<dialog>`.

### Behaviour to know

- Escape fires the dialog's `cancel` event; the hook always calls
  `preventDefault()` so the browser never closes the dialog behind React's back.
- While open, the dialog joins the layer stack shared with `Popover`s. A
  popover left open beneath it neither takes its Escape (the dialog's own
  `cancel` runs) nor closes on a press inside the dialog. A popover opened
  inside the dialog takes Escape before the dialog does.
- A backdrop click counts only when **both** mousedown and mouseup land on the
  `<dialog>` element itself (its content lives in a child). Dragging a text
  selection out of an input onto the backdrop does not dismiss.
- The `<dialog>` must stay mounted. Rendering it conditionally (`{isOpen && <dialog…>}`)
  breaks `showModal()`; its children also stay mounted while closed, so reset
  any form state yourself when reopening.
- A `Select` or `ChipsInput` works inside the modal: their dropdowns render
  inside the open `<dialog>` that contains their anchor (see
  [popover](popover.md)).
- Never call `showModal()` / `close()` yourself.

### Styling

Build the dialog from the recipe styles: `dialog: { ...theme.recipe.modal.dialog }`
(`radius.lg`: the dialog sits on the page), `header`, `body` and `footer` from
`theme.recipe.modal.*`, and pad the body with `theme.space.xxl`. The examples
show it in full.

## Do / don't

- Do pass `canDismiss={!loading}` and also disable the Cancel button while
  loading, so every exit is gated the same way.
- Do keep the `onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}` on the `<dialog>` when it
  is rendered inside a clickable ancestor (a card row); it only stops bubbling,
  dismissal is the hook's job.
- Do wrap the dialog's contents (header, body, footer) in
  [`Surface`](../component/surface.md): hand-drawn boxes are invisible to depth,
  so the Buttons and Selects inside then get the same `md` corners as in a
  `Modal`, with no `radius` or `surface` override.

The hook returns a ref for a `<dialog>` that stays mounted. `isOpen` drives

which closes nothing itself, so it sets `isOpen` to `false`. The `<dialog>` takes
the `theme.recipe.modal.*` styles, and its contents are wrapped in `Surface` so the
Buttons get the corners they would have in a `Modal`. This demo starts open.

The switch holds the busy state on. The `onClick` that stops propagation keeps a
click in the dialog from reaching a clickable ancestor; dismissal is the hook's job.

A `Select` list opens inside the modal and takes Escape before the modal does. The
