changelog.text: **Breaking:** `Dialog` is renamed `Modal` and `useModalDialog` is renamed `useModal`, matching `ConfirmModal`; behaviour is unchanged. The old names `Dialog`, `DialogProps` and `useModalDialog` are removed. The footer marker attribute is now `data-modal-footer`.

Layer stack: popovers and dialogs now close innermost-first. Escape and an outside press only affect the topmost layer, so a popover inside a popover closes one level at a time. **Behaviour change:** a popover beneath an open dialog no longer takes its Escape or closes on a press inside the dialog.
`Popover` renders inside an open `<dialog>` that contains its anchor, so `Select` and `ChipsInput` work in modals.
Every prop has a JSDoc comment, so editors and coding agents see the guidance in the `.d.ts`. `useModalDialog` declares its return type.

guides.title: Corners
guides.description: Corner radius by nesting depth, one radius step per level.
guides.body:
Corner radius tracks **depth**, not size. Surfaces on the page background have
the roundest corners. Each surface nested inside another gets a squarer,
concentric corner, so the inner curve follows the outer one.

## Tokens

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `theme.radius.lg` | 16px | Surfaces on the page background |
| `theme.radius.md` | 8px | One level in: inside a card or modal; also floating layers |
| `theme.radius.sm` | 4px | Two levels in: inside an input, inset box, row, or menu |
| `theme.radius.pill` | 999px | Capsules: nav bar, a Switch with no nearby corner |
| `theme.radius.circle` | 50% | Round glass buttons |

## The rule

Find where the element sits, then read its radius from this table:

| Where the element sits | Radius | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| On the page background | `lg` | `Card`, modal dialog (`recipe.modal.dialog`), and any control directly on a `Page`: `Button`, `Select`, `CardRow`, text fields, `Chip` (automatic) |
| Inside a card or modal | `md` | inputs and their shaded rows, Buttons, Selects, Tags and SegmentedControls in a Card or Modal (automatic), shaded rows (`recipe.row`), inset boxes |
| Inside one of those | `sm` | a chip inside an input, controls in a nested Card, CardRow, inset box (`Surface`) or Popover (automatic), a menu item, a Switch track in a shaded row |
| Flush with its parent (zero inset, edges touch) | the parent's radius | an unlabelled Select's trigger, an input filling its row |
| Inset 4px or less from its parent | `calc(parent − inset)` | a Switch thumb 2px inside a 4px track is 2px |
| A small control with no nearby corner | `pill` / `circle` | a Switch in a full-width card header |
| A floating layer (popover, menu, dropdown, toast) | `md`, plus `shadow.hoverLift` or `recipe.glass` | its items are `sm` |

**Step down one token per level** (`lg` → `md` → `sm`). Do not subtract the
padding: a Card has 13px of inset, but the inputs inside it are `md` (8px), not
16 − 13 = 3px. Exact subtraction applies only to tight insets of 4px or less.

## It's automatic

Components read their corners from the **surface depth** they sit at, so you
pass no radius prop:

| Depth | Radius | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `lg` (16px) | On the page background, inside a `Page` |
| 1 | `md` (8px) | Inside a `Card`, `CardRow`, `Alert` or `Modal` on the page |
| 2+ | `sm` (4px) | One more level in; deeper levels stay `sm` |
| none | each component's old default | No `Page`, `Modal`, `Card`, `CardRow`, `Alert` or `Surface` above it (tests, a component rendered on its own) |

Who provides depth:

- `Page` provides 0, to its header, content and footer actions.
- `Modal` provides 1 to its header, body and footer.
- `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` each provide one level deeper than where
  they sit, so a Card in a Card steps down.
- `Popover` (and so `Menu` and the `Select` list) provides a fixed 2: a
  floating layer is `md` and its items `sm`, whatever opened it.

What follows depth with no prop: `Button`, `Select`, `Card`, `CardRow`,
`Alert`, `TextInput`, `TextArea`, `NumberInput`, `DateTimeInput`,
`ChipsInput` (its chips a step further in), `SegmentedControl`, `Chip`, and a
`Switch` row (`layout="horizontal"`, its `inset` track a step further in). A
field's shaded row and the field in it are flush, so both take the depth
radius. For a hand-made box that holds Buttons or Selects, wrap its contents
in `<Surface>` and read its own radius with `useSurfaceRadius()`; see
[surface](component/surface.md).

Hand-drawn boxes (your own `recipe.card.shell` or `recipe.row` styles, a `useModal` modal) are invisible to depth: wrap their contents in `Surface`.

An explicit prop (`Button radius`, `Select surface`) is an **override** and
always wins over depth. It pins that radius even where depth would step down,
which breaks concentricity, so set it only when the surface really is different
(`radius="background"` on a Button that must stay round inside a Card).

`Switch` still takes `radius` (`inset` or `pill`) by hand for its track;
`inset` follows the row as above, `pill` stays a capsule. `type="link"`
buttons have no padding or background, so radius doesn't apply. Floating
layers (`Toast`, a `Popover` surface, the `ChipsInput` suggestion list) stay
`md` wherever they open.

## In your own styles

```ts
const useStyles = createUseStyles((theme: Theme) => ({
  panel: { ...theme.recipe.card.shell },  // already lg
  inset: {
    backgroundColor: theme.color.bg.cardHeader,
    borderRadius: theme.radius.md,        // one level in
    padding: theme.space.md,
  },
  chip: { borderRadius: theme.radius.sm }, // two levels in
  knob: { borderRadius: `calc(${theme.radius.sm} - 2px)` }, // 2px inset
}));
```

- Never write a literal `borderRadius` (`'12px'`, `'50%'`). The only
  non-token form allowed is `calc(theme.radius.X ± Npx)` for tight insets.
- A 1px inset works the other way too: `Card size="small"` is
  `calc(radius.md + 1px)` so its flush `md` children stay concentric.

guides.title: Patterns
guides.description: How screens are built: forms in cards, confirmations, menus, modals, toasts and style overrides.
guides.body:
How screens are put together from the library, as Bookplate does it.

## A screen

A screen is a `Page` holding a vertical stack of `Card`s, one card per feature.
Page-level buttons sit between the cards with no `radius` prop, because they are
on the page background.

```tsx
import { Page, Card, ThemeSetting } from '@korzun/design/component';
import { Button, Switch } from '@korzun/design/control';

export const SettingsPage = () => (
  <Page back="/" documentTitle="Settings">
    <ThemeSetting />
    <Card title="Notifications">
      <Switch name="digest" label="Email digests" checked={digest} onChange={setDigest} />
    </Card>
    <Button danger onClick={logOut}>Log out</Button>
  </Page>
);
```

## A form in a card

- Fields go in the card body, in a `<Space direction="vertical" gap="md">`. Keep each
  input's default `horizontal` layout (label and control on one shaded row).
- Every field needs a `name`. It is required, and it is the key passed to
  `onValidChange`.
- The submit button goes in the `footer`: `type="primary"`, `submit`, and `form` set to the id of the `<form>` in the body.

```tsx
<Card
  title="Change password"
  footer={
    <Button type="primary" submit form="change-password">Save</Button>
  }
>
  <form id="change-password" action={save}>
    <Space direction="vertical" gap="md">
      <TextInput name="current" label="Current" password value={current} onChange={setCurrent} />
      <TextInput name="next" label="New" password value={next} onChange={setNext} />
    </Space>
  </form>
</Card>
```

## A confirmation

Use `ConfirmModal` for yes/no confirmations. Pass `loading` while the request
is in flight; it disables Cancel and blocks Escape and backdrop dismissal.

```tsx
<ConfirmModal
  isOpen={confirming}
  title="Delete book?"
  confirmText="Delete"
  danger
  loading={deleting}
  onCancel={() => setConfirming(false)}
  onConfirm={remove}
>
  This can't be undone.
</ConfirmModal>
```

## Status banner in a card

An `Alert` inside a `Card` is one step squarer than the Card, and its action
Button one step squarer again. No radius props anywhere.

```tsx
<Card title="Frame">
  <Alert tone="warning" title="Frame is overdue" action={<Button onClick={retry}>Retry</Button>}>
    No check-in for 2h 14m.
  </Alert>
</Card>
```

## Row or card actions menu

Use `Menu` for a list of actions or links behind a button. Spread the trigger
props onto a `Button`; put a link first, and a destructive action last behind
a separator.

```tsx
<Menu
  align="end"
  items={[
    { label: 'Open reader', to: `/books/${id}/read`, Icon: BookIcon },
    { label: 'Delete', onClick: () => setConfirming(true), danger: true, separatorBefore: true },
  ]}
  trigger={(p) => <Button {...p} ariaLabel="Book actions">Actions</Button>}
/>
```

## A custom modal

Use `Modal` for anything that is not a yes/no question: a title, a body, and
an optional footer. Put form errors in the form's `Space` with `ErrorMessage`,
and show loading with `Spinner` (or `loading` on the Button).

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false);
const [error, setError] = useState<string>();

async function save(formData: FormData) {
  setSaving(true);
  setError(undefined);
  try {
    await updateProgress(Number(formData.get('page')));
    setOpen(false);
  } catch {
    setError('Could not save. Try again.');
  } finally {
    setSaving(false);
  }
}

<Modal
  open={open}
  onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  title="Edit progress"
  canDismiss={!saving}
  footer={
    <>
      <Button type="text" onClick={() => setOpen(false)} disabled={saving}>Cancel</Button>
      <Button type="primary" submit form="edit-progress" loading={saving}>Save</Button>
    </>
  }
>
  <form id="edit-progress" action={save}>
    <Space direction="vertical" gap="md">
      <NumberInput name="page" label="Page" value={page} onChange={setPage} />
      <ErrorMessage>{error}</ErrorMessage>
    </Space>
  </form>
</Modal>
```

- A panel that loads on its own shows a `Spinner`:
  `<Space direction="vertical" align="center"><Spinner label="Loading books" /></Space>`.
- Buttons in the footer get Modal's corners from depth; don't set `radius`.
- `Modal` stays mounted: toggle `open`, never render it conditionally.
- Escape and backdrop clicks call `onClose`, unless `canDismiss` is false.
- `Select` and `ChipsInput` work inside a `Modal`.
- Only for a custom native `<dialog>` that `Modal` can't express, build on
  `useModal` (see [use-modal](control/use-modal.md)).

## Notifications

`const toast = useToast()` inside `ToastProvider`. See [toast](toast.md).

## Overriding a library style

Pass `className` (only some components accept it; each module doc says so) and
win specificity with `'&&'`:

```ts
searchButton: { '&&': { borderRadius: theme.radius.md } },
```

Never use `!important`, and never target the library's internal class names.

## Layout and text

Use `Space` for layout and `Text` and `Heading` for text, not
style files. Recipes:

- Body text: a bare `<Text>`; it takes the surrounding look.
- Meta line: `<Text size="sm" tone="muted">`.
- Caption: `<Text size="xs" tone="faint">`.
- Section title: `<Heading level={2}>`.
- Spread row: `<Space justify="between">`.

```tsx
<Space direction="vertical" gap="md">
  <Heading level={2}>Devices</Heading>
  <Space justify="between">
    <Text>Kindle</Text>
    <Text size="sm" tone="muted">Synced today</Text>
  </Space>
  <Text size="xs" tone="faint">Up to five devices.</Text>
</Space>
```

See [space](component/space.md),
[text](component/text.md), and [heading](component/heading.md).

guides.title: Design philosophy
guides.description: The design rules the code enforces, and why.
guides.body:
These are the rules the code already enforces, extracted from the source comments at extraction time. Nothing here is aspirational: each rule names the file whose comment states it and the code that carries it out.

## One modal width

**Rule:** Give every dialog the same width by taking it from `layout.modalWidth`.

**Why:** `src/theme/theme.ts` says "modalWidth: one width for every dialog so modals read as a single system", and `recipe.modal.dialog` reads "One shared width for every modal; the maxWidth keeps it inside a narrow viewport (the auto side-margins then center it)". `layout.modalWidth` is `500px`, and `recipe.modal.dialog` (used by `src/control/confirm-modal/style.ts`) sets `width` to it and caps it at `calc(100vw - space.xxl * 2)`.

## Stacked shadows, not blur, on cards and buttons

**Rule:** Lift cards and buttons with a hard offset shadow (`0px 2px 0px <colour>`), not a blurred one.

**Why:** `src/theme/theme.ts` defines `shadow.cardStack`, `shadow.dangerStack` and `shadow.brandStack` as `0px 2px 0px` with a translucent colour, and `recipe.card.shell` and the button types in `src/control/button/style.ts` use them. Blurred shadows are kept for glass chrome (`shadow.glass`, `shadow.glassActive`, via `recipe.glass` and `recipe.glassHighlight`) and for floating surfaces, which take `shadow.hoverLift`: the toast (`src/toast/style.ts`) and the select and chips-input dropdowns (`src/control/select/style.ts`, `src/control/chips-input/style.ts`). `shadow.card` (`0 1px 3px`) is also blurred; it is defined in `src/theme/theme.ts` but no consumer outside it was found. In dark mode the stacks switch to `applyTransparency('#000', 0.4)`.

## Translucent hover scrims

**Rule:** Paint hover state with a translucent scrim (`color.bg.hover`), never an opaque grey.

**Why:** `src/theme/theme.ts` (`color.bg.hover`, light mode): "A translucent scrim, not an opaque grey: hover has to read on whatever surface it lands on. The old '#f0f0f0' was lighter than the modal footer (gray[100]) it was painted over, so hovering a text button there produced no visible change at all." Light mode is black at 0.07 opacity, dark mode white at 0.12. `src/control/button/style.ts` and `src/control/menu/style.ts` both use it.

## A 16px floor on mobile form controls

**Rule:** Keep the font size of every input, textarea and select at 16px on mobile.

**Why:** `src/theme/global-styles.ts`: "iOS Safari auto-zooms when a form control with a font-size below 16px is focused. Enforce a 16px floor on mobile so focusing an input never zooms." Controls whose class-level font size out-specifies that global rule restore the floor themselves: `recipe.input` in `src/theme/theme.ts` ("Restore the 16px floor on mobile: this class-level font-size otherwise out-specifies the global `input` rule") and `src/control/chips-input/style.ts`.

## Glass chrome with a solid fallback

**Rule:** Build floating chrome from `recipe.glass`, which must degrade to a near-opaque fill where backdrop blur is unavailable.

**Why:** `recipe.glass` in `src/theme/theme.ts` blurs and saturates the backdrop with `color.bg.glass`, and inside `@supports not ((backdrop-filter: blur(1px)) or (-webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(1px)))` swaps the background to `color.bg.glassFallback` (0.92 opacity against 0.6 for the glass itself). `src/control/menu/style.ts`, `src/control/page-actions-menu/style.ts` and `src/control/back-button/style.ts` spread it. `recipe.glassHighlight` is the pressed or active counterpart, used by `src/component/nav-mobile/style.ts`.

## The `track` token must read against both `page` and `card`

**Rule:** Keep `color.bg.track` distinguishable from `color.bg.page` and from `color.bg.card` in both themes.

**Why:** `src/theme/theme.ts` documents `bg.track` as "The rail behind a segmented control's sliding lens. Its own token, not `cardHeader`, because it must read against BOTH `page` and `card` — and in dark mode those sit on either side of `cardHeader`, which left the rail invisible on the page." In light mode it is `gray[100]`; in dark mode it is `#2C2D31`, "A step LIGHTER than the page, not darker", because the dark palette puts `page` above `card` and recessing the track has nowhere to go. `src/control/segmented-control/style.ts` paints it.

## Recipes are spreadable fragments, not components

**Rule:** Express shared styling as a `Recipe` object that styles spread (`...theme.recipe.glass`), not as a component.

**Why:** `src/theme/theme.ts`: "Recipes are JSS-spreadable fragments. Loose typing lets them include pseudo-selectors (`&:hover`) and nested rules without fighting JSS's TS surface." The `Recipe` type is deliberately loose for the same reason. `recipe.input`, `focusRing`, `label`, `spinner`, `glass`, `glassHighlight`, `row`, `modal.*` and `card.*` are all plain objects, and consumers such as `src/control/button/style.ts` spread them (`...theme.recipe.focusRing`).

## Measured layout numbers live in tokens

**Rule:** Put a measured layout number in `theme.layout` (or `theme.size`) and read it from there.

**Why:** `src/theme/theme.ts` on `layout`: "Intrinsic sizes of chrome that other elements must lay out around. These are measured, not derived (the element's real height comes from its content), so they need on-device tuning — keep the single source of truth here." `navHeightMobile` is read by `src/component/page/style.ts` and `src/toast/style.ts`, and `controlHeight` by the text, number, select and date-time inputs. Exception to know about: `src/component/page/style.ts` keeps its own measured `minHeight: '2.25rem'` on `headerRow`, commented "MEASURED, not derived, and the one number to tune here", and `src/control/chips-input/style.ts` uses the same `2.25rem` for its roomier default. Those two have not been promoted to tokens.

## Form controls share one height

**Rule:** Give single-line inputs, selects and chips the same height from `layout.controlHeight`.

**Why:** `src/theme/theme.ts`: "controlHeight: the shared single-line height for inputs/select/chips (~33px) so form controls line up on one row. Single source of truth." `layout.controlHeight` is `2.0625rem`, and `src/control/text-input/style.ts`, `number-input`, `select` and `date-time-input` set `height` to it. `chips-input` uses it only in its `dense` mode.

## Pin floating controls with sticky positioning, not scroll listeners

**Rule:** Hold floating mobile controls in a `position: sticky` row at `layout.floatingControlTopBase`; do not drive a fixed element's `top` from scroll events.

**Why:** `src/component/page/style.ts` (`controlsRow`): "STICKY, not fixed: it starts in the page's flow … scrolls up with the page like everything else, and pins at `floatingControlTopBase` once it gets there." The old approach, a `position: fixed` row with a scroll listener rewriting `top`, "lags the compositor on iOS and jitters for the whole ride; sticky positioning is the same motion, done by the scroller itself." `floatingControlTopBase` in `src/theme/theme.ts` is also the one token that is a position rather than a size.

## Page content clears the floating mobile nav through one token

**Rule:** Anything that must rest above the floating mobile nav adds `layout.navHeightMobile` to its offset instead of hard-coding the nav's height.

**Why:** `src/theme/theme.ts`: "The floating mobile nav capsule is ~96px tall on-device … page padding and bottom-docked toasts both clear it via this token." `src/component/page/style.ts` (`bottomNav`) pads the last row by it "so the last row can always be scrolled above both the nav and Safari's expanded URL bar", and `src/toast/style.ts` rests mobile toasts at `calc(navHeightMobile + space.md + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`.

## Toasts slide up from behind the nav

**Rule:** Stack mobile toasts one layer below the nav (`zIndex.sticky - 1`), so they emerge from behind it rather than covering it.

**Why:** `src/toast/style.ts`: "Rest just above the floating bottom nav (plus the home-indicator inset). Sit one layer below the nav so toasts slide up from behind it, not over it." On mobile the code sets `zIndex: theme.zIndex.sticky - 1`; the desktop container uses `theme.zIndex.toast`.

## Safe-area insets are spent once, by whatever is topmost

**Rule:** Add `env(safe-area-inset-top)` once, at the topmost element, and let anything below it reuse the inset through `--page-top-inset`.

**Why:** `src/component/page/style.ts`: "The inset belongs to whatever is topmost. When that is this `<main>` the fallback applies; when the admin's library-switcher band sits above it, the band has already spent the inset and sets `--page-top-inset` to zero on everything after it." Counting it twice left a status-bar-sized hole in the installed app only, "because in a Safari tab the inset is zero, which is how it went unnoticed." The page's top padding is `calc(space.xxxxxl + var(--page-top-inset, env(safe-area-inset-top)))`. The modal recipe applies the same insets to its mobile margins.

## Un-tokenized literals are declared, not hidden

**Rule:** When a style keeps a literal that is off the token scale, say so in a comment at the top of the file and on the line.

**Why:** `src/control/button/style.ts` opens with "A small handful of literals stay un-tokenized in this file by design", listing `'#FFF'` (focus-ring border on colored backgrounds), `'0.5em'` (a gap that scales with the button's own font size) and `'0.80rem'` (button-specific size, "off the global fontSize scale"). The `0.80rem` line repeats the note in place.

## Not found in the code

- **Ink-on-paper register over glossy chrome.** Searched `src/` for gradients and glossy treatments. The only gradient is a `linear-gradient` mask in `src/component/top-fade/style.ts`, which is a blur fade, not paint. The statement itself lives in Bookplate's `brand/README.md` ("a gradient reads as glossy app-store chrome, which is the opposite of the idea"), where it governs the logo kit (solid ink tiles, `currentColor` marks), and that kit is not part of this package. The flat, hard-edged look the principle implies is covered by the stacked-shadow rule above, so it is not written separately.

guides.title: Tokens
guides.description: Every theme token key in detail, group by group.
guides.body:
Every token lives in `src/theme/theme.ts`. The `Theme` interface declares the groups; `lightTheme` and `darkTheme` are both built by `buildTheme(mode)` and share every key, differing only in values. Consumers read tokens with `useTheme()` or inside `createUseStyles((theme: Theme) => ...)`. The groups below follow the order of the `Theme` type; the key lists are taken from it.

The top-level `colorScheme` key holds the mode, `'light'` or `'dark'` (type `ThemeMode`), and is also the only non-group key of the type.

## color

Surfaces, text, borders and state colours, mode-aware. Keys are grouped as follows.

- `color.gray`: primitive palette, steps `50 100 150 200 300 400 500 600 700 900`. Identical in both modes.
- `color.blue`: primitive palette, steps `50 100 200 300 400 500 600 700 800`. Identical in both modes.
- `color.red`: primitive palette, steps `50 100 300 400 500 600 700`. Identical in both modes.
- `color.text`: `primary secondary muted faint onPrimary onDanger description`
- `color.bg`: `page card cardHeader track switchOff input footer glass glassFallback glassActive selected hover success placeholder`. `track` must read against both `page` and `card`; `switchOff` is an unchecked Switch track, 3:1 on `page`, `card` and `cardHeader`; `hover` is a translucent scrim; `glass*` feed `recipe.glass`.
- `color.border`: `default strong light focus hover danger glass glassActive faint loading success section`. `light` is the hairline rule inside a card or between rows, a step on `page` and `card` in both modes (dark 1.24:1 and 1.39:1, light 1.15:1 and 1.21:1).
- `color.success`, `color.warning`, `color.info`: a single value each.
- `color.brand`: `default hover active light outline loading loadingHover loadingActive linkHover`
- `color.danger`: `default hover active light outline loading loadingHover loadingActive`
- `color.overlay`: `backdrop`
- `color.chip`: thirteen tinted colourways, each `{ text, bg, border }`. Status tones: `success warning danger info neutral`. Label tones: `status author series subject book entryType user rating` (the `status` label tone is not a status tone). `neutral` text holds 4.5:1 on its own tint over `page`, `card` and `cardHeader` in both modes. See Slated for curation.

## space

The spacing scale, in `rem`: `xxxs xxs xs sm md lg xl xxl xxxl xxxxl xxxxxl` (`0.1rem` up to `2rem`).

## radius

Corner radii: `sm md lg circle pill` (`4px`, `8px`, `16px`, `50%`, `999px`).

## layout

Intrinsic sizes of chrome that other elements must lay out around. They are measured, not derived, so they are tuned on a device and kept in one place. Keys: `navHeightMobile` (the floating mobile nav, `96px`), `modalWidth` (the one width for every dialog, `500px`), `formWidth` (a standalone form column such as sign-in, `400px`), `controlHeight` (the shared single-line control height, `2.0625rem`), and `floatingControlTopBase`, a position rather than a size: the `top` at which the mobile back button and actions menu pin, `max(space.xxxl, env(safe-area-inset-top) + space.xxxxl)`.

## fontSize

The type scale: `xxs xs sm md lg xl xxl` (`0.6rem` up to `1.75rem`).

## fontFamily

Two stacks: `body` (`system-ui, sans-serif`) and `mono`.

## fontWeight

Numeric weights: `regular medium semibold bold extrabold` (400, 500, 600, 700, 800).

## lineHeight

Two values: `tight` (1) and `body` (1.3).

## shadow

Mode-aware elevation. `card` is a soft one-pixel shadow (defined, with no consumer outside the theme); `cardStack`, `dangerStack` and `brandStack` are the hard `0px 2px 0px` offset shadows for cards and buttons; `hoverLift` is the elevation of floating surfaces (the toast and the select and chips-input dropdowns); `glass` and `glassActive` belong to `recipe.glass` and `recipe.glassHighlight`. Keys: `card cardStack hoverLift dangerStack brandStack glass glassActive`.

## transition

Shorthand durations and easings: `fast medium slide slow spring`.

## zIndex

Stacking layers: `behind base stack header sticky toast`, where `stack` is a nested `{ lo, md, hi }` (1, 2, 3). Values run from `-1` (`behind`) to `9999` (`toast`).

## breakpoint

Media-query strings, ready to use as JSS keys: `mobile` (`@media (max-width: 640px)`) and `normal` (`@media (min-width: 641px)`).

## recipe

JSS-spreadable style fragments (`...theme.recipe.x`), not components.

- `recipe.input`: the base text-field look (border, radius, hover and focus colours, 16px font on mobile).
- `recipe.focusRing`: a transparent 2px outline that controls recolour on focus.
- `recipe.label`: form label text, with a `$danger` variant.
- `recipe.spinner`: a 1em rotating indicator using the `theme-rotation` keyframes.
- `recipe.glass`: frosted, blurred chrome with a solid fallback where backdrop blur is unsupported.
- `recipe.glassHighlight`: the active or pressed fill that sits on top of glass.
- `recipe.row`: the shaded field row (`bg.cardHeader` fill, `radius.md`, padding `space.md space.lg space.md space.sm`) that `Switch`'s horizontal layout uses; spread it for any custom row that sits beside form fields in a card.
- `recipe.modal.dialog`: the shared dialog shell (one width, backdrop, mobile margins and safe-area insets).
- `recipe.modal.header`: dialog title row.

recipes.title: Copy button
recipes.description: A button that copies text, turns into Copied or Could not copy for two seconds, and announces the result.
recipes.body:
A button that puts text on the clipboard and says what happened. Copy the
`CopyButton` component into your app and pass it the `text` to copy.

## Why it's built this way

- **A recipe, not a `Copy` component.** Where the button sits, what it copies
  and how it looks beside it change from place to place; the state machine is
  the only shared part, and it is short enough to own. `CodeBlock` carries the
  same logic for its own `copyable` button.
- **Three states.** Idle shows `Copy`. A successful write shows `Copied` with a
  `CheckIcon` prefix, and a failed one shows `Could not copy`; both return to
  idle after two seconds. Pressing again restarts the two seconds.
- **No toast.** The answer belongs where the press happened. A toast would
  appear away from the button and pile up if pressed repeatedly.
- **A `role="status"` region.** A label that changes in place is not reliably
  announced, so a visually hidden status region says `Copied` or `Could not
  copy`. It is always mounted, because a region added together with its text is
  often missed. The idle `ariaLabel` is dropped while the label shows the
  result, so the button's name never contradicts the announcement.
- **A missing clipboard counts as a failure.** `navigator.clipboard` is absent
  outside a secure context (a dev server on a LAN address), and `writeText` can
  reject when permission is denied; both show `Could not copy` and throw
  nothing.
- **Clean up on unmount.** One timer is cleared on every press and on unmount,
  and a write that settles after unmount does nothing.

## Keeping the width steady

`Copied` is wider than `Copy`, so a row with the button in the middle would
shift every time it changed. Either put the button last in its row, or give it a
`minWidth` in `em` wide enough for the longest label, `Could not copy` (`10em`
here; `Copied` with its check is shorter). `em` follows the button's font size, so it stays right if
the size changes.

## Wiring it up

- Pass the exact text to copy; the button's label never has to match it.
- For code, `CodeBlock` with `copyable` already includes this button.

recipes.title: Sign in
recipes.description: A centred sign-in card with the submit inside it and Forgot password? on the page below.
recipes.body:
A whole sign-in screen: a card with the two fields and a full-width submit,
and a secondary action on the page below it. Copy the code, then replace the
stubbed action with your auth call.

## Why it's built this way

- **One column, `formWidth` wide.** `theme.layout.formWidth` (`400px`) sets the
  column; `maxWidth: '100%'` lets it shrink inside the page gutter on a phone.
  The card and the button below it are both as wide as the column. See
  [tokens](../tokens.md).
- **Two gaps.** The fields sit `md` apart; Sign In sits `xxl` below them, and
  the card sits `xxl` above Forgot password?. The larger gap separates the
  action from what it acts on.
- **The submit is inside the `<form>`.** It is `type="primary" submit`, so Enter
  in either field submits, and it shows its spinner by itself while the form
  action runs; no `loading` state to manage.
- **Forgot password? is outside the form and the card.** It can't submit, and on
  the page background it is a secondary action, not part of the form.
- **No radius props.** The card is on the page, so it takes the page radius;
  Sign In is one level in, so it is a step squarer; Forgot password? is on the
  page again and matches the card. See [corners](../corners.md).
- **`autoComplete` on both fields.** `username` and `current-password` let
  password managers fill the form; keep them when you adapt it.
- **No label, placeholder only.** On a screen that does one thing the
  placeholders are enough, as in Bookplate.

## Wiring it up

- Replace `signIn` with your auth call. It can read the fields from state, or
  take the `FormData` the action receives (`formData.get('username')`).
- Report failures with a toast (`useToast()`, type `error`): "Invalid
  credentials", "Too many attempts", "Network error". See [toast](../toast.md).
- Without email sign-in, use the placeholder `Username` and drop Forgot
  password?.

recipes.title: Reading progress
recipes.description: A book's progress as "Not started", a ProgressCircle, or "Completed".
recipes.body:
Words for the two ends and a circle for everything between: "Not started"
before the first page, "Completed" after the last, and a `ProgressCircle` with
its percentage in between. Copy the `ReadingProgress` component into your app
and pass it a 0–1 `value` and the book's `title`.

## Wiring it up

- `value` is a fraction from 0 to 1. Divide a 0–100 API percentage by 100
  first, or pass `max={100}` to the circle and change the two checks.
- The end states are plain text, so screen readers read them as they are; the
  circle in between is a named progressbar.
- Change the words or the end states to suit the thing in progress ("Queued",
  "Done", or a check icon at the end).

entries.text: New `Anchor` (control): a page outline from `items` (`{ id, title, level }`) that highlights the section in view and scrolls to one on click. `variant="list"` is an indented list of titles; `variant="minimap"` is a column of dashes that opens the list in a panel on hover or focus, as in Notion. `offset` allows for sticky chrome; it never changes the URL.

New `Space`: one layout primitive with a `direction` (default `'horizontal'`), `gap`, `align`, `justify`, `wrap`, `as` and a `split` separator drawn between items (hidden from screen readers, an `li` inside a list). Each direction keeps Stack's or Inline's defaults.

**Breaking:** `Stack` and `Inline` (and `StackProps`, `InlineProps`) are removed; use `Space`. `<Stack …>` is `<Space direction="vertical" …>` and `<Inline …>` is `<Space …>`, with every prop and default unchanged.

While loading, an `inset` (squared) switch shows a rounded-square ring with an arc travelling around it in the thumb's place, instead of the round spinner, which clashed with its square corners. A `pill` switch keeps the round spinner.

**Breaking:** `ProgressIndicator` is renamed `ProgressCircle` (`ProgressIndicatorProps` → `ProgressCircleProps`). It always draws the circle and writes a number, 0 and 1 included; "Not started" and "Completed" are gone from the component and live in the new Reading progress recipe. The whole mark, label included, is now one `progressbar` with `aria-valuetext`.

New props: `tone` (`brand`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `neutral`; new `ProgressCircleTone` type), `variant="outline"` for a border-only arc instead of the filled pie, `label` (`outside`, `inside`, `none`) for where the value is written, and `max` and `unit` for values that are not fractions (`value={3} max={12} unit=" of 12"` shows "3 of 12").
New recipe: Reading progress, "Not started", a `ProgressCircle` or "Completed" for a book.

**Breaking:** `Tag` is renamed `Chip` (`TagProps` → `ChipProps`, `TagTone` → `ChipTone`), so it shares a name with `ChipsInput` and the `color.chip` tokens it draws from. Props and look are unchanged.
**Breaking:** `chipColor` is renamed `tone` and takes a `ChipTone`, as `Chip` does; the `ChipColor` type is removed (use `ChipTone` from `@korzun/design/component`).
A `disabled` field hides its chips' remove (×) buttons instead of showing them dimmed, so the chips read as plain values.

The text field shares a line with the chips whenever 8rem is free. Before, it sized from an input's natural width (about 20 characters, ~200px at the 16px phone size) and dropped to its own empty line, making the box a line taller than its chips need.
Docs site: the overview thumbnails for `Page`, `Surface`, `TopFade`, `Modal`, `ConfirmModal` and every hook are drawn with plain blocks, like `Space`, instead of sample content.
Docs site: each section lists its modules alphabetically by name, on the overview and in `llms.txt`.

**Breaking:** `isStandalone()` is now the hook `useIsStandalone()`, built on `useSyncExternalStore`. Call it at the top of a component and branch on its value (`const standalone = useIsStandalone();` then `{standalone && <TopFade />}`), not inside a condition or callback. It re-renders when the display mode changes and returns `false` during server rendering instead of throwing on `window`.
Docs generator: CHANGELOG tags that name a removed former name (`CardDivider`, `Dialog`, `useModalDialog`) resolve to the current name, so that history stays on the renamed module's page.

New `prefix`: a decorative icon component drawn inside the field's left end (`prefix={SearchIcon}`) in `text.muted`, with the text moved clear of it. It is hidden from screen readers and lets clicks through. With a clearing `action` it makes a search box (new Search field example).

`separator=""` now counts as unset (gaps, no empty cells); a separator longer than one character logs a development-only console warning once, since it overflows its cell; the separator clip uses logical properties, so right-to-left lines clip and place the separator correctly.

**Breaking:** without `separator` the items are spaced by gaps (`space.lg`, lines `space.sm`), not dots; pass `separator="·"` for the old look. `separator` takes any one character, drawn by CSS between items. Items can now be labelled pairs, `{ label, value }`, shown with a faint capitalized label, mixed with plain items; a pair whose value is `null`, `undefined` or `false` is skipped. New `MetaLineItem` and `MetaLinePair` types. MetaLine replaces `MetadataList`.

**Breaking:** `MetadataList` (and its `Metadata` and `MetadataListProps` types) is removed; use `MetaLine` with `{ label, value }` items and no `separator` for its gapped, labelled look, wrapped in `Text size="sm"` for its size (MetaLine inherits font size and colour; MetadataList set `fontSize.sm` and `text.primary`). Its 15rem cap on each value is gone, and a pair with an empty value is skipped instead of showing its label alone.
**Breaking:** `size.metadataValue` (and the `size` group) is removed; `MetadataList` was its only user.

New `Table` (component): a generic data table. `columns` name a row field or `render` a cell, `rowKey` is a field name or a function, and `empty` shows one full-width row when there are no rows. It scrolls inside its own bordered box on a wide screen (`minWidth` sets a minimum width there only), and on a phone each row stacks with every value labelled by its column title (`label`, `wide`). `nowrap`, `align: 'end'` and `width` shape the cells. Its corners follow surface depth, and a control in a cell sits one level deeper. Falsy values (`0`, `false`, `''`) show as themselves; only `null` and `undefined` show a dash.

New `CodeBlock` (component): a block of code in mono type on a `bg.cardHeader` box that scrolls sideways (with a fade at the edge while more is hidden) or wraps with `wrap`. `code` is the plain text; `children` replace what shows (highlighted spans) while Copy still copies `code`. `copyable` adds a Copy button that becomes Copied with a check, or Could not copy, for 2 seconds and announces it in a status region; `copyLabel` names it. It sets the `--code-*` variables Shiki's css-variables theme emits, from `color.code`. Corners follow surface depth, and in dark mode directly on a Page it gets a 1px `border.default` edge.

New `Code` (component): inline `<code>` in the mono font at 0.875em of the surrounding text (so it scales in a heading), on a `bg.cardHeader` chip with `sm` corners; a long name breaks only when it cannot fit. In dark mode directly on a Page it gets a 1px `border.default` edge. Takes `children` and `className`.

New `color.code` palette (foreground, keyword, string, function, parameter, constant, punctuation, comment, link) for syntax colours, and `recipe.codeBlock`, `recipe.inlineCode` and `recipe.codeColours` (the ten `--code-*` variables Shiki's css-variables theme reads, from `color.code`) for code rendered outside `CodeBlock` and `Code`.

**Breaking:** the `success` prop is removed. It only tinted a `default` button green (a `primary` one stayed blue), which read as a fourth kind of button. For a done state such as Copy turning into Copied!, change the label and add a `CheckIcon` prefix. The `color.bg.success` and `color.border.success` tokens stay. The Button examples now show every type, and `danger` on both `default` and `primary`.

A `link` button's spinner and `prefix`/`suffix` icons sit 0.5em from the label and centred on the text, like the other types; before they touched the label and sat high on the baseline. An icon-only link gets no extra space.

`GlobalStyles` (rendered by `ThemeProvider`) ships the reset the components are drawn against: every element is `box-sizing: border-box` with no default margin or padding, as in Bookplate's and Scribe's `index.html`. Without it a text field was 51px tall instead of `layout.controlHeight` (33px). An app that already carries this reset sees no change; one that relied on browser default margins (`p`, `h1`, `ul`) loses them.

Corners follow surface depth, like `Button` and `Select`: `lg` directly on a `Page`, `md` in a Card or Dialog (unchanged), `sm` two or more levels in (a nested Card, a `CardRow` or `Surface` in a Card, a Popover). A field's shaded row and the field in it take the same radius; `ChipsInput` chips and a horizontal `Switch`'s `inset` track are a step squarer than their box. With no surface above, each keeps its 0.6.0 look. **Visible changes:** fields and Tags placed directly on a Page get 16px corners, and Tags inside a `CardRow` in a Card get 4px. A text field, `ChipsInput` box or field label directly on a Page also moves its text 16px in from the edge (8px elsewhere), the inset `Button` keeps, so it clears the deeper corner.

`color-scheme` is set on `html` as well as `body`. With body alone the root's scheme was `normal`, so in dark mode the page scrollbar stayed light and an iframe whose document uses `GlobalStyles` (or is still loading) painted an opaque white box.

Docs site: the tokens page shows every theme group (`size`, `fontFamily`, `fontWeight` and `lineHeight` were missing), draws one swatch for a single colour (`color.success`), and keeps long token names clear of their values; props and token tables stack each row on a phone instead of scrolling sideways; overview thumbnails stay hidden until they load, so nothing flashes white; a Guides page lists the guides, the header links to it, and the header marks the current section on component, recipe and guide pages; overview and recipe card descriptions render their inline markdown; examples keep their buttons, menu triggers and segmented controls at their own width instead of stretching across the demo.
Docs site: the overview search box has a search icon and, while it holds text, a Clear search button inside its right end (the TextInput `action` pattern) that empties it and returns focus to it.

Segments set their own font size (`fontSize.md`, the 14px of their labels) instead of the browser's 13.33px button default. Labels look the same; the segment's own text metrics no longer depend on the browser or page.
`text` and `link` buttons show a solid 2px `border.focus` ring on keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`); before they showed nothing. Mouse clicks still leave no ring.

Height no longer follows an inherited line-height: Buttons in a Dialog footer are 32px, not 35px, and an icon-only Button is 32px (was 31px, sitting 1px low) beside text Buttons. The label's line-height is pinned to 14px; `link` stays text-sized.

The unchecked track is the new `color.bg.switchOff` token (`#868686` light, `#6E7480` dark), about 3:1 on `bg.page`, `bg.card` and `bg.cardHeader`; it was `border.default` (1.16:1 on a shaded row). The loading spinner on an unchecked track is now the thumb colour.

The option list matches `Menu`: a 4px inset pad, 4px-rounded options with a 2px gap, 14px text (was 12.8px), the flat `cardStack` shadow (was `hoverLift`) and `bg.hover` on hover (was `bg.cardHeader`). The keyboard highlight is unchanged.
Docs: a Copy button recipe (`docs/recipes/copy-button.md`): a `CopyButton` to copy into your app, with Copy, Copied and Could not copy states, a status region and a steady width.

Docs site: each module has an `examples/preview.tsx` that shows the component alone; the overview thumbnails render it instead of the first example, and it never appears on the component page or in the doc. `npm run docs:check` fails for a module without one.

Docs site: one type scale. Markdown and page headings match at each level (h2 20px bold, h3 16px semibold, same spacing), so example, props and changelog titles are no longer smaller than the text under them; code in a heading takes the heading size; page intros are 18px leads. Code blocks and the import line are 14px with a 1.5 line height, inline code is 0.875em and breaks only between words, and every code span uses the theme mono font. Guide, changelog and usage prose stops at 720px while tables and code blocks keep the full width. Props tables are 14px with semibold prop names, muted types, sized columns, and unions that wrap between members.

Dark `color.border.light` is `#333439` (was `#2B2C30`, 1.10:1 on `bg.page` and 1.23:1 on `bg.card`, so hairline rules all but vanished); it is now 1.24:1 and 1.39:1, at or above light mode's step. A loading `Select`'s border in dark is a shade lighter. Light is unchanged.

`color.chip.neutral` text is a step stronger, so a neutral Tag or chip holds 4.5:1 on its tint over `bg.page`, `bg.card` and `bg.cardHeader`: light `#5E5E5E` (was `#6E6E6E`, 4.0:1 over `cardHeader`), dark `#A8ADB6`, the mode's `text.description` (was `#9CA1AB`, 4.47:1 over `page`). Fill and border are unchanged.

Docs site, dark and phones: code blocks and inline code on the page draw a `border.default` edge in dark, where their fill was 1.01:1 on the page; the "–" for an empty props or token cell is muted, not faint (3.7:1). On a phone the header is two rows (name and theme, then links that scroll sideways) and sticks to the top, with headings and tables stopping below it; header links, the theme segments, "Show code" and "Copy" have 44px hit areas, with the desktop look unchanged; the overview is a list with small thumbnails (5,300px tall, was 12,800px); and code that scrolls sideways fades out at its right edge until scrolled to the end.

Docs site: the first Dialog, ConfirmModal, useModalDialog, Popover, Menu and Select example starts open, without taking the page's keyboard focus; readouts sit under their triggers on every page; layout, surface and radius examples share one muted caption style; horizontal-form labels line up; the TextInput and TextArea validation examples open invalid; the Inline wrap, TopFade, ChipsInput chip colours, Divider actions, Inline gaps and Tag tone examples show their point at a glance, and native elements in examples are styled from tokens; an empty overview search offers Clear search; the not-found page uses the site column and link style; changelog entries drop their bullets for a hairline between entries.

`CardDivider` is now `Divider` and works anywhere: directly in a Card or Dialog body it reaches the edges as before (cancelling `space.xl` in a large Card, 1px in a small one, `space.xxl` in a Dialog, where it used to overhang everything but a large Card), and on the page, in a `CardRow`, `Alert`, `Surface` or nested Card it spans its container. The new `bleed` prop overrides that. **Breaking:** the old names `CardDivider`, `CardDividerProps` and `CardDividerAlign` are removed; import `Divider`, `DividerProps` and `DividerAlign`.

**Breaking:** `Dialog` is renamed `Modal` and `useModalDialog` is renamed `useModal`, matching `ConfirmModal`; behaviour is unchanged. The old names `Dialog`, `DialogProps` and `useModalDialog` are removed. The footer marker attribute is now `data-modal-footer`.

Docs: modules are grouped into Layout, Navigation, Typography, Inputs, Overlays, Data display, Feedback, Foundations and Hooks. Actions is gone (`Button` is in Inputs, the Page action bars are in Layout under `Page`), Theme and the icons are Foundations, and the hooks have pages of their own with runnable examples (they were a guide). `PageActionsBar`, `PageActionsMenu` and `PageFooterActions` are listed under `Page` and `CardRow` under `Card`; their pages link to the parent. The overview shows only top-level modules; a nested one appears under Parts on its parent's page, and the overview's search still finds it. The order lives in `scripts/docs-gen/categories.mjs`.

Docs site: props, token and recipe tables render through `Table`, and code through the library: example code, the import line and alias types are `CodeBlock`s, and markdown code blocks and inline code use `recipe.codeBlock` and `recipe.inlineCode` with `color.code` highlighting. Code blocks are padded `space.xl` everywhere (example code was `space.xxl`). Copy buttons on the site show Copied with a check, or Could not copy, in the button for 2 seconds and announce it in a status region, instead of a toast.

Docs: each hook has its own page in the Hooks section, `isStandalone` (`docs/hooks/is-standalone.md`), `useMinimizeOnScroll` (`docs/hooks/use-minimize-on-scroll.md`, with `EXPAND_AFTER`, `MINIMIZE_SPEED` and `MinimizeOnScroll`) and `usePullToRefresh` (`docs/hooks/use-pull-to-refresh.md`, with `PULL_THRESHOLD`, `PullPhase`, `PullState` and the indicator recipe), each with its own examples, types and changelog; `docs/hooks.md` and the `#/components/hooks` page are gone. Imports from `@korzun/design/hooks` are unchanged. `useModal` is listed under Hooks too, though it is still imported from `@korzun/design/control`.
New `theme.layout.formWidth` (`400px`): the width of a standalone form column such as sign-in, narrower than a dialog.
Recipes: worked assemblies of library parts with live previews, shipped as `docs/recipes/*.md` and indexed in AGENTS.md. First recipe: Sign in (`docs/recipes/login.md`).

The visible `label` is linked to its field (`htmlFor` and a generated `id`), so it names the field and clicking it focuses the field. A new `ariaLabel` prop names a field that has no visible `label`; with a `label` it is ignored.
`action` works: clicking its icon button calls `action.action`. `TextInputAction` gains an optional `ariaLabel` naming that button.

Clicks and Enter/Space inside an action no longer reach the header, so no action toggles the section and a native button or link keeps its key press. Actions sit in a `display: contents` wrapper, so the layout is unchanged.
A `value` that is not a finite number (`NaN`, `undefined`, `Infinity`) shows "Not started" instead of "NaN%".

Docs: every module doc has front matter and generated import, examples, props, tokens and changelog sections; prop notes moved into JSDoc; docs site with overview, component pages, llms.txt and llms-full.txt replaces the story gallery. The props types of `Card`, `CardRow`, `CollapsibleSection`, `ConfirmModal`, `Page` and `Button` declare `children` explicitly, so it has a doc line; the types are equivalent, no change for callers.
`ToastProviderProps` is exported from `@korzun/design/toast`.
The popover wrapper carries `data-preferred-side` (the `side` you asked for) alongside `data-side` (the side used after flipping).

Surface depth: corners are concentric site-wide with no radius props. `Page` provides depth 0, `Dialog` 1, and `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` each provide one level deeper than where they sit; `Popover` (so `Menu` and the `Select` list) provides a fixed 2. Depth 0 is `radius.lg`, 1 is `md`, 2 and deeper is `sm`. `Button`, `Select`, `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` follow it; an explicit `Button radius` or `Select surface` still wins. With no `Page`, `Dialog`, `Card`, `CardRow`, `Alert` or `Surface` above it, a component keeps its 0.4.0 look; a bare `Card` (no `Page`) still counts as depth 0 and gives its contents depth 1, so its Buttons and nested Cards change as below.

**Visible changes:**
  - Buttons in a Card default to 8px (they were 16px unless `radius="card"` was set), and Buttons in a Dialog body are 8px.
  - Selects directly on a Page get the page look (16px and the card shadow); in a Card or Dialog they stay 8px. This includes Selects in your own boxes on a Page (a `useModalDialog` modal, a `recipe.card.shell` or `recipe.row` box), because depth cannot see hand-drawn boxes: wrap their contents in `Surface`, or pass `surface="card"`.
  - Without a Page, a bare `Card` counts as depth 0: its Buttons go from 16px to 8px, a Card nested in it steps down, and a `CardRow` in it is 8px.
  - A Card nested in a Card or Dialog steps down (8px, then 4px), and so do its Buttons and Selects; `size="small"` keeps its extra 1px.
  - `CardRow` is 16px on a Page and 8px inside a Card (it was always 16px).
  - Buttons and Selects inside a Popover or Menu are 4px.

New `Alert` (component): a tinted box with a `tone` (`warning`, `danger`, `success`, `info`), optional `title`, `Icon` and `action`, and body text. `danger` and `warning` get `role="alert"`, `success` and `info` get `role="status"`.

New `Surface` and `useSurfaceRadius` (component) for hand-made boxes that hold library controls: `Surface` marks its children one level deeper, and `useSurfaceRadius()` returns the radius token for the current depth.
`Select` `surface` gains `'inset'` (`radius.sm`, no shadow), used two or more levels deep.

`theme.space` values are typed as `SpaceValue` (`${number}rem`), so `gap={theme.space.sm}` on `Popover` and `Menu` needs no `as PopoverGap` cast. `Theme['space']` is now typed `${number}rem`, so hand-built Theme objects or mocks with `px` values stop type-checking.
The internal `ButtonRadiusContext` is removed; Dialog footer Buttons are unchanged (8px).

Guidance: AGENTS.md rule 3 now says not to pass `radius` or `surface` by default; `corners.md` replaces "Picking the prop" with "It's automatic"; new docs for `Alert` and `Surface`; `patterns.md` has a status banner recipe; examples no longer set `radius="card"` or `radius="modal"`.

New `Menu` (control): a button that opens a list of actions and links, described as an `items` array (`onClick` for actions, `to` for links; `Icon`, `danger`, `disabled`, `separatorBefore`, `intentProps`). Arrow keys, Home and End move between items, and Escape returns focus to the trigger. `surface` is `solid` or `glass`.

`Menu` trigger props: `ref` is a callback ref, so it attaches to a `<button>`, an `<a>` or a `Button` without a cast; `ariaControls` is set only while the menu is open. Tab from an open menu skips inert, hidden and `tabindex="-1"` elements and stays inside an open `<dialog>`. A disabled link item has no `href`.

Layer stack: popovers and dialogs now close innermost-first. Escape and an outside press only affect the topmost layer, so a popover inside a popover closes one level at a time. **Behaviour change:** a popover beneath an open dialog no longer takes its Escape or closes on a press inside the dialog.
`Popover` `gap` also accepts a `px` or `rem` string (type `PopoverGap`: `` number | `${number}px` | `${number}rem` ``), not only a number of pixels.

`Button` takes a `ref` and `ariaHasPopup`. Its interactive `<div role="button">` now defaults to `tabIndex={0}` so it is reachable by keyboard (`-1` when disabled or loading; an explicit `tabIndex` wins). Its keydown now calls `preventDefault()` on Enter and Space, so Space no longer scrolls the page and Enter opening a menu does not also activate its first item.

`PageActionsMenu` and `PageActionsBar` are rebuilt on `Menu`: arrow keys, Home and End move between actions, and Escape returns focus to the trigger. `PageActionItem` is now `MenuActionItem & { primary?, align? }`: it gains an optional `Icon` (shown in the menus, ignored by the bar's primary Buttons), and `to` is not allowed.
Guidance: AGENTS.md has a new rule 8 (Menus; later rules renumber to 9–11) and `patterns.md` now teaches `Menu`, and `docs/control/menu.md` is new.
New `Dialog` (control): a modal with a title, body and optional footer on a native `<dialog>`; `canDismiss` blocks Escape and backdrop dismissal while busy.
New `ErrorMessage` (component): a `role="alert"` danger-coloured error line that renders nothing when empty.
New `Spinner` (component): a loading indicator that takes the surrounding text colour and size.
`ConfirmModal` is rebuilt on `Dialog`. No API or visual change; it is now named by its title (`aria-labelledby`).
`Popover` renders inside an open `<dialog>` that contains its anchor, so `Select` and `ChipsInput` work in modals.

Buttons in a `Dialog` footer default to `radius="modal"`; an explicit `radius` still wins. The radius applies to the footer only (a Dialog nested in a footer is unaffected), and `footer={false}`, `''` and `null` render no footer bar.
Guidance: AGENTS.md rules 3, 7 and 10 and the imports table, and `patterns.md`, now teach `Dialog`, `ErrorMessage` and `Spinner`; `Dialog` is no longer listed as missing.

New `Stack` (vertical flex column; `gap`, default `md`), `Inline` (horizontal row; `gap` default `sm`, `justify` including `between`), `Text` (`size`, `tone`, `weight`; unset props inherit), and `Heading` (`level` 1–4), so layout and text are set with props instead of style files.
New `fontWeight.regular` (400) token.
`truncate` on `Text` and `Heading` clips inside `Stack` (any `align`), `Inline`, and a `Stack` nested in an `Inline`; `Stack` and `Inline` roots have `min-width: 0`.

AGENTS.md rule 1 now says layout and text go through these props; rule 10 no longer lists Stack, Text and Heading as things to build yourself, and `patterns.md` and `theme.md` now teach the components.
No visual change to existing components.

`Tag` status tones: `success`, `warning` (yellow, stronger fill), `danger`, `info` (brand blue). New `color.warning` and `color.info` solid colours. Status tones report state; label tones name things. No visual change to existing tags.

`Popover`:
  - `side` (`bottom`/`top`) and `align` (`start`/`center`/`end`).
  - Flips when the preferred side has no room.
  - Stays inside the viewport horizontally, unless `matchWidth` (then it lines up with the anchor exactly).
  - On the top side it is anchored by its bottom edge, and it re-measures when its content resizes (`ResizeObserver`), so it stays attached as content grows or shrinks.
  - The provisional first render is transparent rather than hidden, so an `autoFocus` child takes focus.
  - Exposes `data-side`.
  - Escape calls `onClose` unless already handled, without closing a surrounding dialog.
  - Defaults keep the same position when there is room below; `Select` and `ChipsInput` now open upward near the bottom of the viewport.
New types: `PopoverSide`, `PopoverAlign`.

`CardRow` drops its off-scale `12px` corner and takes `radius.lg` from the card shell, since a row sits on the page background. Its stories now render it on the page, not inside a `Card`. **Visible change:** the corners get rounder (12px to 16px).
`Card size="small"` writes its corner as `calc(radius.md + 1px)`: md plus its 1px inset, concentric with its flush `md` children. Same 9px as before, now derived from the token.
New `theme.recipe.row`: the shaded field row (`bg.cardHeader`, `radius.md`, padding `md lg md sm`), for custom rows beside form fields. `Switch`'s horizontal layout now uses it and looks the same.

New type exports for prop values: `ButtonTypeValue`, `ButtonRadiusValue`, `ChipColor`, `SegmentedOption`, `SwitchRadiusValue`, `TextInputAction`, `CardDividerAlign`, `PageTypeValue`.
Every prop has a JSDoc comment, so editors and coding agents see the guidance in the `.d.ts`. `useModalDialog` declares its return type.

No code changes. `TagTone` type exported from the package root and `/component`.
